title.zh: 卷一百七十六 志第一百二十九 食貨上四
title.raw: 卷一百七十六 志第一百二十九 食貨上四 Volume 176 Treatises 129: Finance and Economics 1d

sentences.zh: 食貨上四

translations.literal: Finance and Economics, Part Four.
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part Four

sentences.zh: （屯田常平義倉）〉

translations.literal: (Military Colonies, Ever-Normal Granaries, and Charity Granaries))
translations.idiomatic: (Military Colonies, Ever-Normal Granaries, and Charity Granaries))

sentences.zh: 前代軍師所在，有地利則開屯田、營田，以省饋餉。

translations.literal: In former ages, wherever armies and commanders were stationed, if the terrain was advantageous they would open military colonies and garrison farms to economize on provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier dynasties, wherever armies were posted, favorable ground was turned into military colonies and garrison farms to cut the cost of supplying the troops.

sentences.zh: 宋太宗伐契丹，規取燕薊，邊隙一開，河朔連歲繹騷，耕織失業，州縣多閑田，而緣邊益增戍兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong of Song campaigned against the Khitan, planning to seize Yan and Ji, once the border was opened the Hebei region suffered disturbances year after year; plowing and weaving were disrupted, many prefectures and counties had idle fields, while border garrisons were steadily increased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong of Song marched against the Khitan with an eye to Yan and Ji, the frontier was thrown open and the Hebei region was unsettled year after year. Farming and weaving collapsed, idle land accumulated in the prefectures and counties, and border garrisons only grew larger.

sentences.zh: 自雄州東際於海，多積水，契丹患之，不得肆其侵突；

translations.literal: From Xiongzhou eastward to the sea there was much standing water, which troubled the Khitan and prevented them from launching their raids at will;
translations.idiomatic: East of Xiongzhou as far as the sea lay extensive flooded ground that checked the Khitan and kept them from raiding freely;

sentences.zh: 順安軍西至北平二百里，其地平曠，歲常自此而入。

translations.literal: from Shun'an Army west to Beiping for two hundred li the land was level and open, and every year they usually entered by this route.
translations.idiomatic: but from Shun'an Army west to Beiping for two hundred li the country was flat and open, and the invaders usually came in along that corridor every year.

sentences.zh: 議者謂宜度地形高下，因水陸之便，建阡陌，浚溝洫，益樹五稼，可以實邊廩而限戎馬。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated said that one ought to gauge the terrain's high and low points, take advantage of water and land routes, lay out field boundaries, dredge canals and ditches, and plant more of the five grains, so as to fill the border granaries and hem in the barbarian horses.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers argued that the land should be surveyed for height and slope, waterways and roads used to advantage, fields laid out, canals dug, and the five grains planted more widely—thereby stocking the border granaries and blocking the enemy cavalry.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，分命左諫議大夫陳恕、右諫議大夫樊知古為河北東、西路招置營田使，恕對極言非便。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, Chen Shu, Left Remonstrance Grand Master, and Fan Zhigu, Right Remonstrance Grand Master, were separately appointed commissioners to recruit and establish garrison farms on the eastern and western routes of Hebei; Shu remonstrated at length that it was inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: In 989, Chen Shu and Fan Zhigu were appointed to organize garrison farms on the eastern and western Hebei circuits respectively; Chen Shu argued forcefully in audience that the plan was ill-advised.

sentences.zh: 行數日，有詔令修完城堡，通導溝瀆，而營田之議遂寢。

translations.literal: After several days on the road, an edict ordered the repair of castles and forts and the clearing of canals and ditches, and the proposal for garrison farms was then laid aside.
translations.idiomatic: A few days into their mission an edict came ordering them instead to repair fortifications and clear waterways, and the garrison-farm scheme was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時又命知代州張齊賢製置河東諸州營田，尋亦罷。

translations.literal: At the same time Zhang Qixian, prefect of Daizhou, was ordered to organize garrison farms in the prefectures of Hedong; this too was soon abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Zhang Qixian, prefect of Daizhou, was told to organize garrison farms across Hedong, but that effort was soon abandoned as well.

sentences.zh: 六宅使何承矩請於順安砦西引易河築堤為屯田。

translations.literal: Palace Service Commissioner He Chengju requested that west of Shun'an Stockade the Yi River be led in and dikes built for a military colony.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengju, commissioner of the Six Residences, proposed diverting the Yi River west of Shun'an Stockade and building dikes for military-colony fields.

sentences.zh: 既而河朔連年大水，及承矩知雄州，又言宜因積潦蓄為陂塘，大作稻田以足食。

translations.literal: Before long the Hebei region suffered great floods year after year; when Chengju became prefect of Xiongzhou he again said that the accumulated floodwater ought to be stored in ponds and reservoirs and rice fields greatly expanded to secure food supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Floods then struck the Hebei region year after year. When He became prefect of Xiongzhou he urged storing the floodwater in ponds and developing rice paddies on a large scale to feed the region.

sentences.zh: 會滄州臨津令閩人黃懋上書言：「閩地惟種水田，緣山導泉，倍費功力。

translations.literal: It happened that Huang Mao of Min, magistrate of Linjin in Cangzhou, submitted a memorial saying: "In Min we plant only wet-field rice, leading springs down from the mountains at double the labor.
translations.idiomatic: About then Huang Mao of Fujian, magistrate of Linjin in Cangzhou, memorialized: "In Fujian we grow only wet rice, channeling springs down from the hills at twice the usual labor.

sentences.zh: 今河北州軍多陂塘，引水溉田，省功易就，五三年間，公私必大獲其利。

translations.literal: Now the prefectures and armies of Hebei have many ponds; drawing water to irrigate fields saves labor and is easy to accomplish—in three to five years both public and private interests will surely reap great profit."
translations.idiomatic: Here in Hebei the garrisons already have many ponds. Irrigating from them would take less work and succeed quickly; within three to five years both the state and the people would profit greatly."

sentences.zh: 」詔承矩按視還，奏如懋言。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Chengju to inspect on site and report back; he memorialized that it was as Mao had said.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered He Chengju to inspect the ground and report; his memorial confirmed Huang Mao's assessment.

sentences.zh: 遂以承矩為製置河北沿邊屯田使，懋為大理寺丞充判官，發諸州鎮兵一萬八千人給其役。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengju was made commissioner to organize military colonies along the Hebei border, Mao was made assistant judge as a clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, and eighteen thousand garrison troops from the various prefectures were mobilized for the work.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengju was then appointed commissioner for border military colonies in Hebei, with Huang Mao as his assistant judge from the Court of Judicial Review, and eighteen thousand troops from the border garrisons were assigned to the project.

sentences.zh: 凡雄莫霸州、平戎順安等軍興堰六百里，置斗門，引澱水灌溉。

translations.literal: In all, from Xiong, Mo, Bazhou, Pingrong, Shun'an, and other armies they raised dikes for six hundred li, set sluice gates, and led the waters of the Baiyang Marshes for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: Dikes six hundred li long were built across Xiong, Mo, Bazhou, Pingrong, Shun'an, and neighboring commands, with sluice gates installed to draw water from the Baiyang Marshes for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 初年種稻，值霜不成。

translations.literal: The first year they planted rice, but frost came and the crop failed.
translations.idiomatic: The first year's rice planting was ruined by an early frost.

sentences.zh: 懋以晚稻九月熟，河北霜早而地氣遲，江東早稻七月即熟，取其種課令種之，是歲八月，稻熟。

translations.literal: Mao said that late rice ripens in the ninth month; in Hebei frost comes early yet the soil's warmth is slow, while in Jiangdong early rice ripens in the seventh month—he took its seed and ordered it planted by quota; that year in the eighth month the rice ripened.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mao noted that late rice ripens in the ninth month: Hebei frosts early though the soil warms slowly, whereas early rice in the lower Yangtze ripens in the seventh month. He brought seed from the south and had it planted under quota; that year the rice ripened in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 初，承矩建議，沮之者頗眾；

translations.literal: At first, when Chengju made his proposal, those who discouraged it were quite numerous;
translations.idiomatic: When He Chengju first proposed the scheme, many spoke against it;

sentences.zh: 武臣習攻戰，亦恥於營葺。

translations.literal: military officers trained in attack and battle were also ashamed of construction and repair work.
translations.idiomatic: and career officers, bred for combat, were ashamed to be put to building and ditch work.

sentences.zh: 既種稻不成，群議愈甚，事幾為罷。

translations.literal: Once the rice planting failed, the crowd's objections grew fiercer and the project nearly came to an end.
translations.idiomatic: After the failed rice crop opposition swelled, and the whole project nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 至是，承矩載稻穗數車，遣吏送闕下，議者乃息。

translations.literal: At this point Chengju loaded several cartloads of rice ears, sent an official to deliver them to the court, and the disputants then fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengju then sent several cartloads of rice ears to the capital by official courier, and the critics fell silent.

sentences.zh: 而莞蒲、蜃蛤之饒，民賴其利。

translations.literal: Moreover, the abundance of bulrushes, cattails, and clams allowed the people to rely on this profit.
translations.idiomatic: The wetlands also yielded rich harvests of reeds, rushes, and shellfish on which the people came to depend.

sentences.zh: 度支判官陳堯叟等亦言：「漢、魏、晉、唐於陳、許、鄧、潁暨蔡、宿、亳至於壽春，用水利墾田，陳跡具在。

translations.literal: Chen Yaosou and others, fiscal commissioners of the Revenue Section, also said: "In Han, Wei, Jin, and Tang, from Chen, Xu, Deng, and Ying through Cai, Su, Bo, and on to Shouchun, they used waterworks to open farmland—the traces of their work all remain.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yaosou and other fiscal commissioners of the Revenue Section also argued: "From Han through Tang, Chen, Xu, Deng, Ying, Cai, Su, Bo, and as far as Shouchun had been brought under cultivation by water control—the evidence is still there.

sentences.zh: 議選官大開屯田，以通水利，發江、淮下軍散卒及募民充役。

translations.literal: It is proposed to select officials and greatly open military colonies, extend waterworks, and mobilize scattered soldiers from lower Yangtze and Huai armies together with recruited civilians for the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Officials should be chosen to reopen military colonies on a large scale, restore the waterways, and assign scattered troops from the Jiang-Huai commands plus recruited civilians to the work.

sentences.zh: 給官錢市牛、置耕具，導溝瀆，築防堰。

translations.literal: Give official funds to purchase oxen and set out farming tools, guide canals and ditches, and build protective dikes.
translations.idiomatic: State funds would buy oxen and tools, canals would be dug, and protective dikes built.

sentences.zh: 每屯十人，人給一牛，治田五十畝，雖古制一夫百畝，今且墾其半，俟久而古制可復也。

translations.literal: Each colony would have ten men, each man given one ox, cultivating fifty mu of fields; although the ancient system allotted one hundred mu per husbandman, for now let us open half of that—after long years the ancient system can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Each colony would hold ten men, each with one ox and fifty mu under cultivation. The ancient allotment was one hundred mu per man; for the present half that would suffice, and the full measure could be restored in time.

sentences.zh: 畝約收三斛，歲可收十五萬斛，七州之間置二十屯，可得三百萬斛，因而益之，數年可使倉廩充實，省江、淮漕運。

translations.literal: Each mu would yield about three hu; annually one could harvest one hundred fifty thousand hu; placing twenty colonies among the seven prefectures would yield three million hu; expanding from this, within several years the granaries could be filled and Jiang-Huai transport costs saved.
translations.idiomatic: At roughly three hu per mu, annual yield would reach one hundred fifty thousand hu; twenty colonies across the seven prefectures would produce three million hu, and further expansion in a few years could fill the granaries and spare the Jiang-Huai grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 民田未辟，官為種植，公田未墾，募民墾之，歲登所取，並如民間主客之例。

translations.literal: Where private fields were not yet opened, the state would plant for them; where public fields were not yet reclaimed, civilians would be recruited to reclaim them; the annual harvest taken would all follow the civilian host-and-guest precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Unopened private land would be planted by the state; unreclaimed public land would be opened by recruited tenants; and the annual levy would follow the usual landlord-tenant shares.

sentences.zh: 傅子曰：『陸田命懸於天，人力雖修，苟水旱不時，則一年之功棄矣。

translations.literal: Master Fu said: 'Dry-field farming depends on Heaven's decree; though human effort may be applied, if flood and drought come untimely, a year's labor is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu wrote: "Dry farming hangs on the weather: no matter how hard men work, untimely flood or drought wastes a year's effort.

sentences.zh: 水田之制由人力，人力苟修，則地利可盡。

translations.literal: The system of wet-field farming rests on human effort; if human effort is applied, the land's advantage can be fully realized.
translations.idiomatic: Wet rice depends on human labor; where labor is steady, the land's full yield can be had.

sentences.zh: 』且蟲災之害亦少於陸田，水田既修，其利兼倍。

translations.literal: ' Moreover, the harm of insect plagues is also less than with dry fields; once wet fields are developed, the profit is doubled besides.
translations.idiomatic: " Insect damage is lighter than on dry land, and once wet fields are in order the return is twice as great."

sentences.zh: 」帝覽奏嘉之，遣大理寺丞皇甫選、光祿寺丞何亮乘傳按視經度，然不果行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor read the memorial and approved it, sending Huangfu Xuan, clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, and He Liang, clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, post-haste to inspect and plan on site—yet in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial and sent Huangfu Xuan and He Liang on fast courier to survey the ground, but the plan was never executed.

sentences.zh: 至咸平中，大理寺丞王宗旦請募民耕潁州陂塘荒地凡千五百頃。

translations.literal: By the Xianping era, Wang Zongdan, clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, requested recruiting civilians to farm a total of fifteen hundred qing of pond and waste land in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping period, Wang Zongdan asked that civilians be recruited to farm fifteen hundred qing of pond and waste land in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 部民應募者三百餘戶，詔令未出租稅，免其徭役。

translations.literal: More than three hundred households in the district answered the call; an edict ordered that until rent and tax were due, their corvée labor be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Over three hundred households answered the call; an edict exempted them from corvée until rent and tax came due.

sentences.zh: 然無助於功利。

translations.literal: Yet it did not help practical benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme brought little practical gain.

sentences.zh: 而汝州舊有洛南務，內園兵人種稻，雍熙二年罷，賦予民，至是復置，命京朝官專掌。

translations.literal: In Ruzhou there had formerly been the Luonan Office, where inner-garden soldiers planted rice; in the second year of Yongxi it was abolished and assigned to the people; now it was re-established and a capital official was ordered to manage it exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhou had once maintained the Luonan Office, where palace-garden troops grew rice; it was abolished in 985 and the land given to civilians, but now it was restored under a capital official appointed to run it.

sentences.zh: 募民戶二百餘，自備耕牛，立團長，墾地六百頃，導汝水溉灌，歲收二萬三千石。

translations.literal: More than two hundred civilian households were recruited, supplying their own plow oxen; group leaders were appointed; six hundred qing were reclaimed; the Ru River was led in for irrigation; annual harvest was twenty-three thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred tenant households supplied their own oxen; group leaders were appointed; six hundred qing were opened; the Ru River was channeled for irrigation; and the annual harvest reached twenty-three thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 襄陽縣淳河，舊作堤截水入官渠，溉民田三千頃；

translations.literal: At Xiangyang county the Chun River had formerly had dikes built to dam water into the official canal, irrigating three thousand qing of civilian fields;
translations.idiomatic: In Xiangyang county dikes on the Chun River had long diverted water into the official canal to irrigate three thousand qing of private fields;

sentences.zh: 宜城縣蠻河，溉田七百頃；

translations.literal: at Yicheng county the Man River irrigated seven hundred qing;
translations.idiomatic: the Man River at Yicheng county watered seven hundred qing;

sentences.zh: 又有屯田三百餘頃。

translations.literal: there were also more than three hundred qing of military-colony fields.
translations.idiomatic: and there were more than three hundred qing of military-colony land besides.

sentences.zh: 知襄州耿望請於舊地兼括荒田，置營田上、中、下三務，調夫五百，築堤堰，仍集鄰州兵每務二百人，荊湖市牛七百分給之。

translations.literal: Geng Wang, prefect of Xiangzhou, requested that on the old sites waste land also be included, establishing upper, middle, and lower garrison-farm offices; five hundred laborers were mobilized to build dikes and weirs; troops from neighboring prefectures were gathered at two hundred men per office; seven hundred oxen were purchased in Jing-Hu and distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Geng Wang of Xiangzhou asked to add waste land to the old sites and set up upper, middle, and lower garrison-farm offices. Five hundred laborers built dikes and weirs; two hundred troops from neighboring commands were assigned to each office; and seven hundred oxen were bought in Jing-Hu and issued to them.

sentences.zh: 是歲，種稻三百餘頃。

translations.literal: That year, more than three hundred qing of rice were planted.
translations.idiomatic: That year more than three hundred qing of rice were planted.

sentences.zh: 四年，陝西轉運使劉綜亦言：「宜於古原州建鎮戎軍置屯田。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Liu Zong, transport commissioner of Shaanxi, also said: "It is fitting to establish Zhenrong Army at ancient Yuanzhou and set up military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1001 Liu Zong, Shaanxi transport commissioner, also urged establishing Zhenrong Army at old Yuanzhou with military colonies.

sentences.zh: 今本軍一歲給芻糧四十餘萬石、束，約費茶鹽五十餘萬，儻更令遠民輸送，其費益多。

translations.literal: Now this army alone is supplied each year with more than four hundred thousand shi and bundles of fodder and grain, costing about five hundred thousand in tea and salt; if distant civilians were further made to transport, the expense would increase yet more.
translations.idiomatic: The army already consumed over four hundred thousand shi and bundles of fodder and grain a year, costing some five hundred thousand in tea and salt equivalents; forcing distant civilians to haul supplies would only add to the burden.

sentences.zh: 請於軍城四面立屯田務，開田五百頃，置下軍二千人、牛八百頭耕種之；

translations.literal: I request establishing military-colony offices on all four sides of the army city, opening five hundred qing of fields, and setting two thousand lower-army troops and eight hundred oxen to cultivate them;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed military-colony offices around the garrison, five hundred qing opened to cultivation, two thousand lower-army troops and eight hundred oxen assigned to farm them;

sentences.zh: 又於軍城前後及北至木峽口，各置堡砦，分居其人，無寇則耕，寇來則戰。

translations.literal: furthermore, before and behind the army city and north to Mukou Pass, stockades should each be placed and the men distributed among them—when there is no raider they farm, when raiders come they fight.
translations.idiomatic: and stockades before and behind the city and north to Mukou Pass, garrisoning the men so they would farm in peace and fight when raiders came.

sentences.zh: 就命知軍為屯田製置使，自擇使臣充四砦監押，每砦五百人充屯戍。

translations.literal: At the same time appoint the army commander as military-colony organizing commissioner, let him choose envoys to serve as superintendents of the four stockades, and assign five hundred men per stockade as colony garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: The army commander would serve as colony commissioner, choose envoys to supervise the four stockades, and assign five hundred colony troops to each.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 既而原、渭州亦開方田，戎人內屬者皆依之得安其居。

translations.literal: Before long Yuan and Wei prefectures also opened square fields, and barbarians who submitted inward all relied on this to secure their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Wei prefectures soon opened square fields as well, and tribesmen who submitted were able to settle securely.

sentences.zh: 是時兵費浸廣，言屯、營田者，輒詔邊臣經度行之。

translations.literal: At this time military expenses were gradually expanding; whenever anyone spoke of military or garrison farms, the court would promptly order border officials to plan and carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: As military costs mounted, any proposal for military or garrison farms brought orders for border officials to plan and execute it.

sentences.zh: 順安軍兵馬都監馬濟請於靖戎軍東壅鮑河，開渠入順安、威虜二軍，置水陸營田於其側。

translations.literal: Ma Ji, military superintendent of Shun'an Army, requested that east of Jingrong Army the Bao River be dammed, a canal opened into Shun'an and Weilu armies, and land-and-water garrison farms established on its flanks.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ji, military superintendent of Shun'an Army, proposed damming the Bao River east of Jingrong Army, cutting a canal into Shun'an and Weilu, and establishing land and water garrison farms along it.

sentences.zh: 命莫州部署石普護其役，逾年而畢。

translations.literal: Shi Pu, deployment commander of Mozhou, was ordered to oversee the work; after more than a year it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu, deployment commander of Mozhou, was put in charge; the work took more than a year.

sentences.zh: 知保州趙彬復奏決雞距泉，自州西至蒲城縣，分徐河水南流注運渠，廣置水陸屯田，詔駐泊都監王昭遜共成之。

translations.literal: Zhao Bin, prefect of Baozhou, again memorialized opening Jiju Spring, from the prefecture west to Pucheng county, dividing the Xu River so its waters flowed south into the transport canal, and broadly establishing land-and-water military colonies; an edict ordered Stationed Fleet Superintendent Wang Zhaoxun to complete it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bin, prefect of Baozhou, also proposed tapping Jiju Spring and diverting the Xu River south from the prefecture west to Pucheng into the transport canal, with extensive land and water military colonies; Wang Zhaoxun, stationed fleet superintendent, was ordered to help finish the work.

sentences.zh: 自是定州亦置屯田。

translations.literal: From this time Dingzhou also established military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou then established military colonies as well.

sentences.zh: 五年，罷襄州營田下務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the lower garrison-farm office of Xiangzhou was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1002 the lower garrison-farm office at Xiangzhou was abolished.

sentences.zh: 六年，耿望又請於唐州赭陽陂置務如襄州，歲種七十餘頃，方城縣令佐掌之，調夫耘耨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Geng Wang again requested establishing at Zheyang Pond in Tangzhou an office like that at Xiangzhou; more than seventy qing were planted annually; the magistrate and assistants of Fangcheng county managed it and mobilized laborers for hoeing and reaping.
translations.idiomatic: In 1003 Geng Wang asked for a similar office at Zheyang Pond in Tangzhou; more than seventy qing were planted yearly under the Fangcheng magistrate and staff, with corvée labor for hoeing and harvest.

sentences.zh: 景德初，從京西轉運使張巽之請，詔止役務兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, following the request of Zhang Xun, transport commissioner of western capital circuit, an edict ordered that garrison-farm troops not be conscripted for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde period, at the request of Zhang Xun, western capital transport commissioner, an edict forbade drafting garrison-farm troops for corvée.

sentences.zh: 二年，令緣邊有屯、營田州軍，長吏並兼製置諸營田、屯田事，舊兼使者如故。

translations.literal: In the second year it was ordered that in border prefectures and armies with military or garrison farms, the chief officials should all concurrently organize all garrison-farm and military-colony affairs; former concurrent commissioners remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1005 border commands with military or garrison farms were told that their chief officials would concurrently oversee all such farms; existing special commissioners were left in place.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，改定保州、順安軍營田務為屯田務，凡九州軍皆遣官監務，置吏屬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the garrison-farm offices of Baozhou and Shun'an Army were renamed military-colony offices; all nine prefecture-armies were sent officials to supervise the offices and clerical staff were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1016 the garrison-farm offices at Baozhou and Shun'an Army were renamed military-colony offices; supervisors and clerks were posted to all nine border commands.

sentences.zh: 淮南、兩浙舊皆有屯田，後多賦民而收其租，第存其名。

translations.literal: Huainan and the two Zhe circuits had formerly all had military colonies; later most were assigned to the people with rent collected, retaining only the name.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan and the two Zhe circuits had once had military colonies too, but most land was later assigned to civilians for rent while the names alone survived.

sentences.zh: 在河北者雖有其實，而歲入無幾，利在蓄水以限戎馬而已。

translations.literal: Those in Hebei, though they had substance, yielded little annual revenue; the profit lay only in storing water to limit barbarian horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei the colonies still functioned, but annual revenue was slight; the real benefit was impounding water to block enemy cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天禧末，諸州屯田總四千二百餘頃，河北歲收二萬九千四百餘石，而保州最多，逾其半焉。

translations.literal: By the end of Tianxi, military colonies in all prefectures totaled more than four thousand two hundred qing; Hebei annually harvested more than twenty-nine thousand four hundred shi, of which Baozhou had the most, exceeding half.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Tianxi era colonies nationwide totaled over forty-two hundred qing; Hebei yielded over twenty-nine thousand four hundred shi a year, more than half from Baozhou alone.

sentences.zh: 襄、唐二州營田既廢，景德中，轉運使許逖復之。

translations.literal: The garrison farms of Xiang and Tang prefectures having been abolished, during Jingde Transport Commissioner Xu Ti restored them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiang and Tang garrison farms were abolished, transport commissioner Xu Ti restored them during the Jingde period.

sentences.zh: 初，耿望借種田人牛及調夫耨獲，歲入甚廣。

translations.literal: At first Geng Wang borrowed tenant farmers' oxen for planting and mobilized laborers for hoeing and harvest; annual revenue was very large.
translations.idiomatic: At first Geng Wang borrowed tenants' oxen and drafted labor for hoeing and harvest, and revenue was substantial.

sentences.zh: 後張巽改其法，募水戶分耕，至逖又參以兵夫，久之無大利。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Xun changed the method, recruiting water-land households to farm in shares; when Xu Ti came he again mixed in military laborers; after long years there was no great profit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun later changed the rules, recruiting wetland tenants to farm in shares; Xu Ti added troops to the mix; in time little profit remained.

sentences.zh: 天聖四年，遣尚書屯田員外郎劉漢傑往視，漢傑言：「二州營田自復至今，襄州得穀三十三萬餘石，為緡錢九萬餘；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiansheng, Liu Hanjie, outer vice director of the Ministry of Revenue's Colony Section, was sent to inspect; Hanjie said: "From restoration to the present the two prefectures' garrison farms—Xiangzhou has obtained more than three hundred thirty thousand shi of grain, worth more than ninety thousand strings of cash;
translations.idiomatic: In 1026 Liu Hanjie of the Ministry of Revenue's Colony Section was sent to inspect. He reported: "Since restoration, Xiangzhou had produced over three hundred thirty thousand shi of grain, worth more than ninety thousand strings;

sentences.zh: 唐州得穀六萬餘石，為緡錢二萬餘。

translations.literal: Tangzhou has obtained more than sixty thousand shi of grain, worth more than twenty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Tangzhou over sixty thousand shi, worth more than twenty thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 所給吏兵俸廩、官牛雜費，襄州十三萬餘緡，唐州四萬餘緡，得不補失。

translations.literal: Salaries and rations for clerks and troops, official oxen, and miscellaneous expenses—Xiangzhou more than one hundred thirty thousand strings, Tangzhou more than forty thousand strings—the gain did not cover the loss.
translations.idiomatic: But pay, rations, official oxen, and overhead had cost Xiangzhou over one hundred thirty thousand strings and Tangzhou over forty thousand—the accounts showed a net loss.

sentences.zh: 」詔廢以給貧民，頃收半稅。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered abolition and assignment to poor civilians, collecting half tax for a time.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the farms and gave the land to poor civilians at half tax for a period.

sentences.zh: 其後陝西用兵，詔轉運司度隙地置營田以助邊計，又假同州沙苑監牧地為營田，而知永興軍範雍括諸郡牛頗煩擾，未幾遂罷。

translations.literal: Afterward, when Shaanxi was at war, an edict ordered the transport office to survey vacant land and establish garrison farms to aid the border budget; pasture land of Shazhou Pasturage in Tongzhou was also lent for garrison farms; but Fan Yong, prefect of Yongxing Army, requisitioned oxen from various prefectures with considerable disturbance, and before long it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Shaanxi the transport office was told to find spare land for garrison farms to ease frontier costs; pasture at Shazhou in Tongzhou was also lent for the purpose; but Fan Yong of Yongxing Army's roundup of oxen from many prefectures caused such trouble that the scheme was soon dropped.

sentences.zh: 右正言田況言：「鎮戎、原、渭，地方數百里，舊皆民田，今無復農事，可即其地大興營田，以保捷兵不習戰者分耕，五百人為一堡，三兩堡置營田官一領之，播種以時，農隙則習武事。

translations.literal: Right Rectifier Tian Kuang said: "Zhenrong, Yuan, and Wei—several hundred li in territory—were formerly all civilian fields; now farming has ceased. On this land garrison farms could be greatly expanded; Baojie troops unskilled in battle could be divided to farm, five hundred men per stockade, one garrison-farm official over every two or three stockades; sow in season, and in farming intervals practice military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Right Rectifier Tian Kuang proposed: "Zhenrong, Yuan, and Wei cover hundreds of li that were once farmland but lie idle. Garrison farms could be opened there; Baojie troops unfit for battle could farm in groups of five hundred per stockade under one farm officer per two or three stockades, sowing on schedule and drilling in the farming slack season.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，不用。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted and not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 後乃命三司戶部副使夏安期等議並邊置屯田，迄不能成。

translations.literal: Later the court ordered Xia Anqi and others, vice commissioners of the Three Departments' Household Section, to deliberate on establishing military colonies along the entire border, but in the end it could not be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xia Anqi and others of the Three Departments were ordered to plan border-wide military colonies, but nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 治平三年，河北屯田三百六十七頃，得穀三萬五千四百六十八石。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiping, Hebei military colonies totaled three hundred sixty-seven qing, yielding thirty-five thousand four hundred sixty-eight shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1066 Hebei military colonies covered three hundred sixty-seven qing and yielded thirty-five thousand four hundred sixty-eight shi.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，以內侍押班李若愚同提點製置河北屯田事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, Palace Attendant Li Ruoyu, chief of the inner service guard shift, was made co-superintendent to organize Hebei military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining reforms the eunuch Li Ruoyu was made co-superintendent of Hebei military colonies.

sentences.zh: 三年，王韶言：「渭原城而下至秦州成紀，旁河五六百里，良田不耕者無慮萬頃，治千頃，歲可得三十萬斛。

translations.literal: In the third year Wang Shao said: "From Weiyuan city down to Chengjii in Qinzhou along the river for five or six hundred li, uncultivated good fields are no less than ten thousand qing; if one thousand qing were worked, annually three hundred thousand hu could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In 1070 Wang Shao reported: "From Weiyuan city down to Chengjii in Qinzhou along the river for five or six hundred li lie at least ten thousand qing of good land lying fallow; working one thousand qing would yield three hundred thousand hu a year.

sentences.zh: 」知秦州李師中論：「韶指極邊見招弓箭手地，恐秦州益多事。

translations.literal: " Li Shizhong, prefect of Qinzhou, argued: "Shao points to frontier land where mounted archers are being recruited; I fear Qinzhou will have yet more troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Shizhong of Qinzhou objected: "Shao means land on the extreme frontier where mounted archers are being recruited; Qinzhou will only see more trouble.

sentences.zh: 」詔遣王克臣等按視，復奏與師中同。

translations.literal: " An edict sent Wang Kechen and others to inspect on site; they memorialized in agreement with Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Wang Kechen and others to inspect; they agreed with Li Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 再下沈起，起奏：「不見韶所指何地，雖實有之，恐召人耕種，西蕃驚疑。

translations.literal: The matter was referred again to Shen Qi; Qi memorialized: "I do not see which land Shao indicates; though it may truly exist, I fear that summoning people to farm will alarm and unsettle the western Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qi was consulted next and reported: "I cannot tell which land Shao means. Even if it exists, calling in settlers to farm may alarm the western Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 」侍御史謝景溫言：「聞沈起妄指甘穀城弓箭手地以塞韶妄。

translations.literal: " Censor Xie Jingwen said: "I hear that Shen Qi falsely indicated Gangu city mounted-archer land to cover Shao's falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xie Jingwen said: "I hear that Shen Qi falsely cited Gangu city archer land to discredit Shao."

sentences.zh: 」而竇舜卿奏：「實止有閑田一頃四十三畝。

translations.literal: " But Dou Shunqing memorialized: "In fact there is only one qing and forty-three mu of idle land.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Shunqing memorialized: "In fact there is only one qing and forty-three mu of idle land."

sentences.zh: 」中書言：「起未嘗指甘穀城地以實韶奏，而師中前在秦州與韶更相論奏，互有曲直。

translations.literal: " The Secretariat said: "Qi never pointed to Gangu city land to substantiate Shao's memorial, while Shizhong, when previously in Qinzhou, and Shao repeatedly memorialized against each other, each with right and wrong on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat said: "Qi never pointed to Gangu city land to substantiate Shao's memorial, while Shizhong and Shao had long traded accusations in Qinzhou, each with some justice on his side."

sentences.zh: 」韶遂以妄指閑田自著作佐郎責保平軍節度推官，師中亦落待制。

translations.literal: " Shao was therefore demoted from Assistant Archivist to military judge of Baoping Army for falsely indicating idle land; Shizhong also lost his pending appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was demoted from Assistant Archivist to military judge of Baoping Army for falsely claiming idle land; Shizhong lost his pending appointment as well.

sentences.zh: 其後韓縝知秦州，乃言：「實有古渭砦弓箭手未請空地四千餘頃。

translations.literal: Afterward Han Zhen, as prefect of Qinzhou, said: "In fact there is more than four thousand qing of unclaimed vacant land for mounted archers at Guwei Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Zhen as prefect of Qinzhou reported over four thousand qing of unclaimed archer land at Guwei Stockade.

sentences.zh: 」遂復韶故官，從其所請行之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Shao's former office was restored and his request was allowed to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's rank was restored and his proposal approved.

sentences.zh: 明年，河北屯田司奏：「豐歲屯田，入不償費。

translations.literal: The next year the Hebei Military Colony Office memorialized: "In a bumper year the military colonies' revenue does not cover expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Hebei Military Colony Office reported that even in a good year revenue did not cover costs.

sentences.zh: 」於是詔罷緣邊水陸屯田務，募民租佃，收其兵為州廂軍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict abolished the border land-and-water military-colony offices, recruited civilians to rent and tenant the land, and reassigned the troops as prefectural garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Border land and water colony offices were abolished, the land rented to civilians, and the troops reassigned as prefectural garrison soldiers.

sentences.zh: 時陝西曠土多未耕，屯戍不可撤，遠方有輸送之勤，知延州趙禼請募民耕以紓朝廷憂，詔下其事。

translations.literal: At this time much waste land in Shaanxi was still uncultivated; garrison colonies could not be withdrawn, and distant regions bore the labor of transport; Zhao Xu, prefect of Yanzhou, requested recruiting civilians to farm to ease the court's concern; an edict referred the matter downward.
translations.idiomatic: Much of Shaanxi still lay uncultivated while garrisons could not be reduced and distant regions bore heavy transport costs. Zhao Xu, prefect of Yanzhou, asked to recruit civilians to farm and ease the court's burden; the proposal was referred for action.

sentences.zh: 經略安撫使郭逵言：「懷寧砦所得地百里，以募弓箭手，無閑田。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Guo Kui said: "The land obtained at Huaining Stockade extends a hundred li, used to recruit mounted archers; there is no idle land.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Guo Kui replied that the hundred li around Huaining Stockade was already allotted to mounted archers and no idle land remained.

sentences.zh: 」禼又言之，遂括地得萬五千餘頃，募漢蕃兵幾五千人，為八指揮，詔遷禼官，賜金帛。

translations.literal: " Xu pressed again; land was then surveyed totaling more than fifteen thousand qing; nearly five thousand Han and tribal troops were recruited in eight commands; an edict promoted Xu's office and bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xu persisted; a land survey found over fifteen thousand qing; nearly five thousand Han and tribal troops were recruited in eight commands; and Xu was promoted and rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 而熙州王韶又請以河州蕃部近城川地招弓箭手，以山坡地招蕃兵弓箭手，每砦五指揮，以二百五十人為額，人給地一頃，蕃官二頃，大蕃官三頃。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Wang Shao of Xizhou again requested using river-prefecture tribal lands near the city and river valleys to recruit mounted archers, and hillside lands to recruit tribal mounted archers—five commands per stockade, quota of two hundred fifty men, one qing per man, two qing for tribal officers, three qing for senior tribal officers.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao of Xizhou also asked to recruit mounted archers on river-valley land near Hezhou cities and tribal archers on hillsides—five commands per stockade, two hundred fifty men each, one qing per man, two for tribal officers, three for senior tribal officers.

sentences.zh: 熙河多良田，七年，詔委提點秦鳳路刑獄鄭民憲興營田，許奏辟官屬以集事。

translations.literal: Xi-He had much good farmland; in the seventh year an edict entrusted Zheng Minxian, circuit intendant for penal affairs on the Qinfeng route, to establish garrison farms, permitting memorialized recruitment of staff to gather the work.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi-He region had abundant good land; in 1074 Zheng Minxian, Qinfeng circuit penal intendant, was ordered to open garrison farms and allowed to recruit staff by memorial.

sentences.zh: 樞密使吳充上疏曰：「今之屯田，誠未易行。

translations.literal: Councilor of State Wu Chong submitted a memorial saying: "Today's military colonies are truly not easy to implement.
translations.idiomatic: Councilor of State Wu Chong wrote: "Military colonies are hard to run today.

sentences.zh: 古者一夫百畝，又受田十畝為公田，莫若因弓箭手仿古助田法行之。

translations.literal: In antiquity one husbandman had one hundred mu, and additionally received ten mu as public fields; better to follow the mounted archers and implement the ancient aid-field method.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity each man held one hundred mu plus ten mu of public field; better to adapt the ancient aid-field system to the mounted archers.

sentences.zh: 熙河四州田無慮萬五千頃，十分取一以為公田，大約中歲畝一石，則公田所得十五萬石。

translations.literal: The four prefectures of Xi-He have no less than fifteen thousand qing of fields; taking one-tenth as public fields, roughly in an average year one shi per mu, public fields would yield one hundred fifty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The four Xi-He prefectures had at least fifteen thousand qing; a tenth as public fields, at roughly one shi per mu in an average year, would yield one hundred fifty thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 官無屯營牛具廩給之費，借用眾力而民不勞，大荒不收而官無所損，省轉輸，平糴價，如是者其便有六。

translations.literal: The state would have none of the expenses for colony barracks, oxen, tools, and granary rations; borrowing the multitude's strength without tiring the people; in great famine no harvest yet the state suffers no loss; saving transport; leveling purchase prices—such are six conveniences.
translations.idiomatic: The state would avoid colony barracks, oxen, tools, and ration costs; use popular labor without overburdening the people; suffer no loss in famine years; save transport costs; and stabilize grain prices—six advantages in all.

sentences.zh: 」而提點刑獄鄭民憲言：「祖宗時屯、營田皆置務，屯田以兵，營田以民，固有異制。

translations.literal: " But Zheng Minxian, circuit intendant for penal affairs, said: "In the times of our ancestors, military and garrison farms each had offices; military colonies used troops, garrison farms used civilians—the systems were inherently different.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Minxian, penal intendant, said: "Under the founding emperors military colonies used troops and garrison farms used civilians, each with its own office—the two systems had always differed."

sentences.zh: 然襄州營田既調夫矣，又取鄰州之兵，是營田不獨以民也；

translations.literal: Yet at Xiangzhou the garrison farm had already drafted laborers and also took soldiers from neighboring prefectures—thus garrison farms did not rely on civilians alone;
translations.idiomatic: Yet at Xiangzhou the garrison farm drafted corvée labor and still drew troops from neighboring prefectures, so garrison farms were never staffed by civilians alone;

sentences.zh: 邊州營屯，不限兵民，皆取給用，是屯田不獨以兵也；

translations.literal: At border prefectures, garrison colonies drew on both soldiers and civilians without distinction, all being conscripted for use—thus military colonies did not rely on troops alone either;
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier, garrison colonies made no distinction between soldier and civilian and pressed both into service, so military colonies likewise were never manned by troops alone;

sentences.zh: 至於招弓箭手不盡之地，復以募民，則兵民參錯，固無異也。

translations.literal: As for places where mounted archers had not fully been recruited, civilians were recruited again, so soldiers and civilians were intermixed—in substance there was no difference.
translations.idiomatic: Where mounted archers could not fill the quota, civilians were recruited as well; soldiers and civilians were jumbled together, and in practice the two systems amounted to the same thing.

sentences.zh: 而前後施行，或侵占民田，或差借耨夫，或諸郡括牛，或兵民雜耕，或諸州廂軍不習耕種、不能水土，頗致煩擾。

translations.literal: Yet in implementation before and after, sometimes they encroached on civilian fields, sometimes they drafted or borrowed hoeing laborers, sometimes various prefectures requisitioned oxen, sometimes soldiers and civilians farmed together, and sometimes garrison troops of various prefectures were unskilled at planting and could not adapt to local conditions, causing considerable disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated trials the policy brought encroachments on private fields, forced loans of weeding labor, county-wide roundups of oxen, mixed soldier-civilian plowing, and garrison troops who knew nothing of farming or local conditions—altogether a heavy burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 至於歲之所入，不償其費，遂又報罷。

translations.literal: As for what came in each year, it did not cover the expense, and the project was again reported abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Annual yields never matched costs, and the scheme was abandoned once more.

sentences.zh: 惟因弓箭手為助田法，一夫受田百畝，別以十畝為公田，俾之自備種糧功力，歲畝收一石，水旱三分除一，官無廩給之費，民有耕鑿之利，若可以為便。

translations.literal: Only the aid-field method for mounted archers seemed workable: one man received one hundred mu, with ten mu set apart as public fields, obliging him to provide his own seed, grain, and labor; each mu was to yield one shi per year, with one-third remitted in flood or drought; the state would have no granary-ration expense and the people would gain the profit of plowing and opening land—this appeared to be a convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Only the mounted-archer aid-field plan looked promising: each man would hold one hundred mu plus ten mu of public field, supplying seed and labor himself; the levy was one shi per mu yearly, with a third forgiven in flood or drought. The state would avoid granary payouts and the farmers would keep the gains of cultivation—an arrangement that seemed genuinely advantageous.

sentences.zh: 然弓箭手之招至，未安其業，而種糧無所仰給，又責其借力於公田，慮人心易搖，乞候稍稔推行。

translations.literal: Yet when mounted archers were recruited they had not yet settled into their occupations, and had no source from which to obtain seed and grain, while still being charged with labor on the public fields; fearing that people's minds would easily waver, he requested that implementation be deferred until harvests were somewhat abundant.
translations.idiomatic: But the archers, once recruited, had not yet put down roots, lacked seed and provisions, and were already liable for labor on the public fields; lest morale falter, he asked that the plan wait until the land had yielded a few good harvests.

sentences.zh: 」九年，詔：「熙河弓箭手耕種不及之田，經略安撫司點廂軍田之，官置牛具農器，人一頃，歲終參較弓箭手、廂軍所種優劣為賞罰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict said: "For Xi-He mounted archers' fields not yet brought under cultivation, the Pacification and Tranquillization Commission shall assign garrison troops to farm them; the state shall provide oxen, harness, and farm tools, one qing per man; at year's end the plantings of mounted archers and garrison troops shall be compared, with rewards and punishments according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year an edict ordered that until Xi-He archers could work their allotments, the Pacification Commission should detail garrison troops to farm the land, supply oxen, tack, and tools at one qing per man, and at year's end rank archer and garrison yields for reward or penalty.

sentences.zh: 弓箭手逃地並營田召佃租課，許就近於本城砦輸納，仍免折變、支移。」

translations.literal: Abandoned archer land together with garrison-farm fields opened to tenants would be subject to rent levies; payment was permitted at the nearest home fort or stockade, and conversion surcharges and transport diversions were still waived."
translations.idiomatic: Archers' abandoned plots and garrison-farm tenancies would be assessed for rent, payable at the nearest home fort or stockade, with conversion fees and transport diversions waived.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，改定州屯田司為水利司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Dingzhou Military Colony Office was changed to a Hydraulic Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1079 the Dingzhou Military Colony Office was renamed the Hydraulic Office.

sentences.zh: 及章惇築沅州，亦為屯田務，其後遂罷之，募民租佃，役兵各還所隸。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun built Yuanzhou, a military colony commission was also established; afterward it was abolished, civilians were recruited to rent and cultivate the land, and corvée soldiers each returned to their original units.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun fortified Yuanzhou he set up a colony commission too, but it was later abolished; civilians were hired to tenant the fields and the corvée troops sent back to their commands.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔提舉熙河等路弓箭手、營田、蕃部共為一司，隸涇原路製置司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered that the superintendencies over Xi-He route mounted archers, garrison farms, and frontier tribes be combined into one office, subordinate to the Jingyuan route Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082 an edict merged the Xi-He mounted archers, garrison farms, and frontier tribes under one superintendency subordinate to the Jingyuan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 提舉熙河營田康識言：「新復土地，乞命官分畫經界，選知田廂軍，人給一頃耕之，餘悉給弓箭手，人加一頃，有馬者又加五十畝，每五十頃為一營。

translations.literal: Kang Shi, superintendent of Xi-He garrison farms, said: "On newly recovered land, I beg that officials be ordered to demarcate boundaries, garrison troops skilled in farming be selected and given one qing each to cultivate, and the remainder all be allotted to mounted archers with one additional qing per man; those with horses receive fifty mu more; every fifty qing shall form one camp.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Shi, superintendent of Xi-He garrison farms, proposed: "On the newly recovered lands, officials should survey boundaries, assign one qing apiece to garrison troops who know farming, and give the rest to mounted archers at an extra qing per man—fifty mu more for those with horses—forming a camp every fifty qing.

sentences.zh: 」「四砦堡見缺農作廂軍，許於秦鳳、涇原、熙河三路選募廂軍及馬遞鋪卒，願行者人給裝錢二千。

translations.literal: At the four forts and bastions now lacking agricultural garrison troops, selection and recruitment of garrison troops and courier-station soldiers from the Qinfeng, Jingyuan, and Xi-He routes is permitted; those willing to go shall each receive two thousand in outfit money.
translations.idiomatic: Where the four forts and bastions lacked farming garrison troops, he asked to recruit garrison troops and courier-station soldiers from Qinfeng, Jingyuan, and Xi-He, with two thousand cash in outfit money for each volunteer.

sentences.zh: 」詔皆從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved every item.

sentences.zh: 知太原府呂惠卿嘗上《營田疏》曰：「今葭蘆、米脂裏外良田，不啻一二萬頃，夏人名為『真珠山』、『七寶山』，言其多出禾粟也。

translations.literal: Lu Huiqing, prefect of Taiyuan, once submitted a Garrison Farm Memorial saying: "Today the good fields within and beyond Jialu and Mizhi amount to no less than ten or twenty thousand qing; the Xia call them 'Pearl Mountain' and 'Treasure Mountain,' meaning that they produce much grain and millet.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huiqing, prefect of Taiyuan, once memorialized on garrison farms: "The fertile land around Jialu and Mizhi runs to ten or twenty thousand qing at least. The Xia name the region Pearl Mountain and Treasure Mountain for the grain it yields.

sentences.zh: 若耕其半，則兩路新砦兵費，已不盡資內地，況能盡辟之乎？

translations.literal: If half were cultivated, the military expenses of the new forts on both routes would no longer depend entirely on the interior—how much more if all were opened?
translations.idiomatic: Reclaim even half of it and the new frontier forts on both routes would no longer lean wholly on the interior for supplies—let alone if the whole were brought under the plow.

sentences.zh: 前此所不敢進耕者，外無捍衛也。

translations.literal: What had prevented cultivation before was the lack of external defense.
translations.idiomatic: The reason plowing had not been attempted earlier was simply that there was no shield on the outside.

sentences.zh: 今於葭蘆、米脂相去一百二十里間，各建一砦，又其間置小堡鋪相望，則延州之義合、白草與石州之吳堡、剋胡以南諸誠砦，千里邊麵皆為內地，而河外三州荒閑之地，皆可墾辟以贍軍用。

translations.literal: Now, in the hundred and twenty li between Jialu and Mizhi, build one fort in each place and set small bastion posts between them in sight of one another; then Yizhou's Yihe and Baicao together with Shizhou's Wubao and the various forts south of Kehu—a thousand li of border face—will all become interior land, and the idle ground of the three prefectures beyond the river can all be reclaimed to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Build a fort at Jialu and another at Mizhi, a hundred and twenty li apart, with smaller posts between them in mutual view, and from Yizhou's Yihe and Baicao to Shizhou's Wubao and Kehu and the forts beyond—a thousand li of frontier becomes hinterland. The idle lands of the three prefectures across the river could then be opened to feed the armies.

sentences.zh: 凡昔為夏人所侵及蘇安靖棄之以為兩不耕者，皆可為法耕之。

translations.literal: All land formerly invaded by the Xia and abandoned by Su Anjing as land neither side would cultivate may be farmed by this method.
translations.idiomatic: Every field once raided by the Xia and left fallow under Su Anjing's policy of mutual abstention could be planted by this same method.

sentences.zh: 於是就糴河外，而使河內之民被支移者，量出腳乘之直，革百年遠輸貴糴，以免困公之弊。

translations.literal: Thus grain would be purchased on the spot beyond the river, and for people within the river subject to transport diversion, the cost of porterage would be assessed, abolishing a century of costly long-distance transport and dear purchase, so as to avoid the abuse of exhausting the public.
translations.idiomatic: Grain could be bought locally beyond the river, while people within it who had borne transport diversions would be compensated for porterage—ending a hundred years of costly long hauls and ruinous state purchases.

sentences.zh: 財力稍豐，又通葭蘆之道於麟州之神木，其通堡砦亦如葭蘆、米脂之法，而橫山膏腴之地，皆為我有矣。」

translations.literal: When financial strength grew somewhat, the road from Jialu to Shenmu in Linzhou would also be opened, and the connecting bastions and forts would follow the Jialu–Mizhi method; then the fertile lands of Hengshan would all be ours."
translations.idiomatic: As revenues strengthened, the route from Jialu to Shenmu in Linzhou and its chain of posts could follow the same pattern, and the rich soil of Hengshan would be firmly in our hands."

sentences.zh: 七年，惠卿雇五縣耕牛，發將兵外護，而耕新疆葭蘆、吳堡間膏腴地號木瓜原者，凡得地五百餘頃，麟、府、豐州地七百三十頃，弓箭手與民之無力及異時兩不耕者又九百六十頃。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Huiqing hired plow oxen from five counties, dispatched general troops to guard the outer perimeter, and farmed the fertile land called Papaya Plain between newly recovered Jialu and Wubao—altogether more than five hundred qing; land in Lin, Fu, and Feng prefectures seven hundred thirty qing; and for mounted archers and civilians without means and land formerly left uncultivated by both sides, another nine hundred sixty qing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1084 Huiqing hired oxen from five counties, sent regular troops to guard the perimeter, and plowed Papaya Plain, the rich ground between newly taken Jialu and Wubao—over five hundred qing in all, plus seven hundred thirty qing in Lin, Fu, and Feng prefectures and nine hundred sixty qing for archers, poor civilians, and fields long left idle by both sides.

sentences.zh: 惠卿自謂所得極厚，可助邊計，乞推之陝西。

translations.literal: Huiqing claimed the gains were extremely substantial and could aid border finance, and requested that the policy be extended to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing declared the harvest enormous and a boon to frontier finance, and asked that the scheme be spread across Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 八年，樞密院奏：「去年耕種木瓜原，凡用將兵萬八千餘人，馬二千餘匹，費錢七千餘緡，穀近九千石，糗糒近五萬斤，草萬四千餘束；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized: "Last year Papaya Plain was farmed with more than eighteen thousand regular troops and over two thousand horses, at a cost of more than seven thousand strings of cash, nearly nine thousand shi of grain, nearly fifty thousand jin of dried provisions, and more than fourteen thousand bundles of fodder;
translations.idiomatic: In 1085 the Bureau of Military Affairs reported that farming Papaya Plain the previous year had consumed more than eighteen thousand regular troops and two thousand horses, over seven thousand strings of cash, nearly nine thousand shi of grain, fifty thousand jin of field rations, and fourteen thousand bundles of fodder;

sentences.zh: 又保甲守禦費緡錢千三百，米石三千二百，役耕民千五百，雇牛千具，皆強民為之；

translations.literal: community-defense costs came to thirteen hundred strings of cash and three thousand two hundred shi of rice; one thousand five hundred farming civilians were impressed, and one thousand oxen hired—all forced on the people;
translations.idiomatic: community-defense levies added thirteen hundred strings and thirty-two hundred shi of rice; fifteen hundred farmers and a thousand hired oxen had all been wrung from the populace by force;

sentences.zh: 所收禾粟、蕎麥萬八千石，草十萬二千，不償所費。

translations.literal: the grain and millet and buckwheat collected came to eighteen thousand shi and one hundred two thousand bundles of fodder, which did not cover the expense.
translations.idiomatic: the harvest—grain, millet, and buckwheat—totaled eighteen thousand shi and fodder one hundred two thousand bundles, falling short of the outlay.

sentences.zh: 又借轉運司錢穀以為子種，至今未償，增入人馬防拓之費，仍在年計之外。

translations.literal: Grain and cash had also been borrowed from the transport commission for seed and had not yet been repaid; the added cost of men and horses for frontier defense still lay outside the annual budget.
translations.idiomatic: Seed money and grain borrowed from the transport commission remained unpaid, and the extra manpower and horses for frontier defense still sat outside the annual accounts.

sentences.zh: 慮經略司來年再欲耕種，乞早約束。

translations.literal: Fearing that the Pacification Commission would again wish to farm next year, they begged for early restraint.
translations.idiomatic: They feared the Pacification Commission would try planting again the next year and asked that limits be set at once.

sentences.zh: 」詔諭惠卿毋蹈前失。

translations.literal: An edict admonished Huiqing not to repeat his earlier mistake.
translations.idiomatic: An edict warned Huiqing not to repeat his earlier error.

sentences.zh: 河東進築堡砦，自麟石、鄜延南北近三百里，及涇原、環慶、熙河蘭會新復城砦地土，悉募廂軍配卒耕種免役。

translations.literal: Forts and bastions were advanced and built in Hedong from north to south for nearly three hundred li between Linshi and Fuyan, and on the soil of newly recovered cities, forts, and stockades in Jingyuan, Huanqing, and Xi-He Lanzhou and Huizhou, garrison troops and assigned soldiers were all recruited to farm and were exempt from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong pushed forward fortifications for nearly three hundred li from Linshi to Fuyan, and across the newly recovered posts of Jingyuan, Huanqing, and Xi-He Lanzhou and Huizhou garrison troops were recruited to farm with corvée waived.

sentences.zh: 已而營田司言諸路募發廂軍皆不閑田作，遂各遣還其州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Garrison Farm Office reported that garrison troops recruited and dispatched on every route were all unskilled at fieldwork, and they were sent back each to his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Garrison Farm Office reported that recruited garrison troops everywhere were useless in the fields, and each man was sent home to his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，知荊南府解潛奏辟宗綱、樊賓措置屯田，詔除宗綱充荊南府、歸峽州、荊門公安軍鎮撫使司措置五州營田官，樊賓副之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, Xie Qian, prefect of Jingnan, memorialized recommending Zong Gang and Fan Bin to organize military colonies; an edict appointed Gang commissioner for garrison farms in five prefectures under the Jingnan, Guixia, Jingmen, and Gong'an Army Pacification Commission, with Fan Bin as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 Xie Qian, prefect of Jingnan, recommended Zong Gang and Fan Bin to set up military colonies; Gang was made commissioner for garrison farms in five prefectures under the Jingnan pacification command, with Fan Bin as deputy.

sentences.zh: 渡江後營田蓋始於此。

translations.literal: Garrison farms after the crossing of the Yangzi probably began here.
translations.idiomatic: Southern garrison farming likely dates from this moment.

sentences.zh: 其後荊州軍食仰給，省縣官之半二。

translations.literal: Afterward Jingzhou's military provisions relied on them, saving roughly half of what prefecture and county officials had formerly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Jingzhou fed its garrisons from the farms, easing by about half what local officials had once been obliged to furnish.

sentences.zh: 三年，德安府、復州、漢陽軍鎮撫使陳規放古屯田，凡軍士：相險隘，立堡砦，且守且耕，耕必給費，斂復給糧，依鋤田法，餘並入官。

translations.literal: In the third year, Chen Gui, Pacification Commissioner of De'an, Fuzhou, and Hanyang Army, restored the ancient military-colony system: for soldiers—choose defensible ground, erect forts and stockades, guard and farm together; farming required supplying expenses, and at harvest grain was issued again; following the hoe-field law, the surplus all went to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In 1133 Chen Gui, pacification commissioner for De'an, Fuzhou, and Hanyang Army, revived the old colony system. Soldiers were to hold defensible points, build forts, and farm while they guarded; the state paid farming costs and issued grain at harvest under the hoe-field rule, with the surplus to government stores.

sentences.zh: 凡民：水田畝賦粳米一斗，陸田豆麥夏秋各五升，滿二年無欠，給為永業。

translations.literal: For civilians: paddy fields paid one dou of polished rice per mu; dry fields paid five sheng each of beans and wheat in summer and autumn; after two years without arrears, the land was granted as permanent property.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians owed one dou of husked rice per mu on paddy land and five sheng of beans or wheat per mu in each of summer and autumn on dry land; after two years without default the plot became theirs in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 兵民各處一方，流民歸業浸眾，亦置堡砦屯聚之。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians each occupied separate areas; as displaced people returned to their occupations in growing numbers, forts and stockades were also set up to gather them in colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians lived apart; as refugees returned in swelling numbers, forts were also raised to settle them in colonies.

sentences.zh: 凡屯田事，營田司兼之；

translations.literal: All military-colony affairs were jointly handled by the Garrison Farm Office;
translations.idiomatic: Military-colony business fell jointly to the Garrison Farm Office;

sentences.zh: 營田事，府、縣兼之。

translations.literal: garrison-farm affairs were jointly handled by prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: garrison-farm business to prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 廷臣因規奏推廣，謂一夫授田百畝，古制也，今荒田甚多，當聽百姓請射。

translations.literal: Court officials, following Gui's memorial, urged extension, saying that granting one hundred mu to one man was the ancient system; today there is much wasteland and commoners should be allowed to apply to open it.
translations.idiomatic: Following Gui's proposal, court officials urged a wider rollout: one hundred mu per man was the ancient rule, and with wasteland abundant the people should be free to apply to reclaim it.

sentences.zh: 其有闕耕牛者，宜用人耕之法，以二人曳一犁。

translations.literal: Where plow oxen were lacking, the method of human plowing should be used, with two men drawing one plow.
translations.idiomatic: Where oxen were scarce, two men should pull a single plow by hand.

sentences.zh: 凡授田，五人為甲，別給蔬地五畝為廬舍場圃。

translations.literal: For all land grants, five men formed one tithing group, and five mu of vegetable ground were separately given for dwellings, yards, and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Every grant would group five men in a tithing, with five mu of vegetable ground set aside for houses, yards, and gardens.

sentences.zh: 兵屯以大使臣主之，民屯以縣令主之，以歲課多少為殿最。

translations.literal: Military colonies were headed by grand emissary officials, civilian colonies by county magistrates, with annual yields determining merit ratings.
translations.idiomatic: Military colonies would answer to grand emissary officials and civilian colonies to magistrates, ranked by annual yield.

sentences.zh: 下諸鎮推行之。

translations.literal: The order was sent down to the various prefectures for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dispatched to the prefectures for adoption.

sentences.zh: 詔江東、西宣撫使韓世忠措置建康營田，如陝西弓箭手法。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Han Shizhong, Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong and Jiangxi, to organize Jiankang garrison farms on the model of the Shaanxi mounted archers.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong, pacification commissioner of Jiangdong and Jiangxi, was ordered to organize Jiankang garrison farms on the Shaanxi archer model.

sentences.zh: 世忠言：「沿江荒田雖多，大半有主，難如陝西例，乞募民承佃。

translations.literal: Shizhong said: "Along the river there is much wasteland, but most of it has owners; it is hard to follow the Shaanxi precedent; I beg to recruit civilians to tenant it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong replied: "Wasteland is plentiful along the river, but most of it already has owners; the Shaanxi model will not do—I ask instead to recruit civilians to tenant the fields.

sentences.zh: 」都督府奏如世忠議，仍蠲三年租，滿五年，田主無自陳者，給佃者為永業。

translations.literal: The Chief Council memorialized as Shizhong proposed, still remitting rent for three years; after five years, if the landowner did not come forward on his own, the plot would be granted to the tenant as permanent property.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Council agreed, exempting rent for three years and providing that after five years, if the owner did not claim the land, the tenant would receive it in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 詔湖北、浙西、江西皆如之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hubei, Zhexi, and Jiangxi all to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei, western Zhe, and Jiangxi were ordered to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 其徭役科配並免。

translations.literal: Corvée and assessed levies were all waived.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée and special levies were waived entirely.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔淮南、川陝、荊襄屯田。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered military colonies in Huainan, Chuan-Shaan, and Jing-Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1135 an edict extended military colonies to Huainan, Sichuan-Shaanxi, and the Jing-Xiang region.

sentences.zh: 六年，都督張浚奏改江、淮屯田為營田，凡官田逃田並拘籍，以五頃為一莊，募民承佃。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Chief Councilor Zhang Jun memorialized to change Jiang-Huai military colonies into garrison farms; all government fields and abandoned fields were registered and seized, five qing forming one estate, and civilians were recruited to tenant them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1136 Zhang Jun proposed renaming Jiang-Huai military colonies as garrison farms, registering all official and abandoned fields, grouping them into five-qing estates, and recruiting civilian tenants.

sentences.zh: 其法：五家為保，共佃一莊，以一人為長，每莊給牛五具，耒耜及種副之，別給十畝為蔬圃，貸錢七十千，分五年償。

translations.literal: The method was: five households formed one mutual-liability group and jointly tenanted one estate, with one man as head; each estate was given five oxen, with plows and seed to match, ten mu separately granted as a vegetable garden, and seventy thousand cash lent, to be repaid over five years.
translations.idiomatic: Five households would form a mutual-liability group to tenant one estate under a headman; each estate received five oxen, plows, seed, ten mu for vegetables, and a loan of seventy thousand cash repaid over five years.

sentences.zh: 命樊賓、王弗行之。

translations.literal: Fan Bin and Wang Fu were ordered to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bin and Wang Fu were put in charge.

sentences.zh: 尋命五大將劉光世、韓世忠、張俊、岳飛、吳玠及江淮、荊、襄、利路帥悉領營田使。

translations.literal: Soon the five great generals Liu Guangshi, Han Shizhong, Zhang Jun, Yue Fei, and Wu Jie, together with commanders of the Jiang-Huai, Jing, Xiang, and Li routes, were all made garrison-farm commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the five great generals—Liu Guangshi, Han Shizhong, Zhang Jun, Yue Fei, and Wu Jie—along with the Jiang-Huai, Jing, Xiang, and Li route commanders were all named garrison-farm commissioners.

sentences.zh: 遷賓司農少卿，提舉江、淮營田，置司建康，弗屯田員外郎副之。

translations.literal: Bin was transferred to Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs for Agriculture, superintendent of Jiang-Huai garrison farms, with an office at Jiankang; Fu, as outer-sect director of military colonies, served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bin was promoted to vice minister of agriculture and superintendent of Jiang-Huai garrison farms with headquarters at Jiankang; Wang Fu, outer-sect director of military colonies, served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 官給牛、種，撫存流移，一歲中收穀三十萬石有奇。

translations.literal: The state supplied oxen and seed, cared for the displaced, and within one year collected more than three hundred thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: With oxen and seed from the state and care for the displaced, the program harvested more than three hundred thousand shi in a single year.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史石公揆、監中獄李寀及王弗皆言營田之害，張浚亦覺其擾，請罷司，以監司領之，於是詔帥臣兼領營田。

translations.literal: Palace Remonstrance Attendant Shi Gongkui, prison supervisor Li Cai, and Wang Fu all spoke of the harm of garrison farms; Zhang Jun also perceived the disturbance and requested abolishing the office and having surveillance commissioners take charge—whereupon an edict ordered frontier commanders to hold garrison-farm duties concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gongkui, Li Cai, and Wang Fu all denounced the abuses of garrison farming; Zhang Jun too saw the disruption and asked to abolish the dedicated office in favor of surveillance commissioners—whereupon commanders were ordered to oversee garrison farms concurrently.

sentences.zh: 九月，以川陝宣撫吳玠治廢堰營田六十莊，計田八百五十四頃，歲收二十五萬石以助軍儲，賜詔獎諭焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Sichuan-Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie had restored abandoned weirs and run sixty garrison-farm estates totaling eight hundred fifty-four qing, with an annual harvest of two hundred fifty thousand shi to aid military stores, an edict of commendation was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wu Jie, Sichuan-Shaanxi pacification commissioner, was commended by edict for restoring ruined weirs and operating sixty garrison-farm estates on eight hundred fifty-four qing, yielding two hundred fifty thousand shi yearly for army stores.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，督視湖北、京西軍馬汪澈言：「 荊、湖兩軍屯守襄、漢，糧餉浩瀚。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, Wang Che, overseer of Hubei and Jingxi forces, said: "The two armies of Jing and Hu garrison Xiang and Han, and their provisions are vast.
translations.idiomatic: In 1162 Wang Che, overseer of Hubei and Jingxi forces, reported: "The Jing and Hu armies holding Xiangyang and Hanzhong consume provisions on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 襄陽古有二渠，長渠溉田七千頃，木渠溉田三千頃，兵後堙廢。

translations.literal: Xiangyang anciently had two canals: the Long Canal irrigated seven thousand qing and the Wood Canal three thousand qing; after the war they were silted and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang once had two canals—the Long Canal watering seven thousand qing and the Wood Canal three thousand—but both had silted up in the wars.

sentences.zh: 今先築堰開渠，募邊民或兵之老弱耕之，其耕牛、耒耜、種糧，令河北、京西轉運司措置，既省饋運，又可安集流亡。

translations.literal: Now build weirs and open the canals first, recruit frontier civilians or the old and weak among the troops to farm them; oxen, plows, and seed grain shall be arranged by the Hebei and Jingxi transport commissions—thus saving transport while also settling the displaced.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed rebuilding the weirs and clearing the channels, hiring frontier civilians or aged and weak soldiers to farm them with oxen, plows, and seed furnished by the Hebei and Jingxi transport offices—cutting transport costs while resettling refugees.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，臣僚言州縣營田之實，其說有十，曰：擇官必審，募人必廣，穿渠必深，鄉亭必修，器用必備，田處必利，食用必充，耕具必足，定稅必輕，賞罰必行。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, officials spoke of the realities of prefectural and county garrison farms; their program had ten points, namely: choose officials carefully, recruit people broadly, dig canals deeply, repair district posts, equip tools fully, situate fields advantageously, supply food adequately, provide plow implements sufficiently, set taxes lightly, and enforce rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1163 officials laid out ten requirements for sound garrison farming: careful choice of officers, broad recruitment, deep canals, repaired district posts, complete equipment, well-sited fields, ample provisions, sufficient plows, light taxes, and strict rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 且欲立賞格以募人，及住廣西馬綱三年以市牛。

translations.literal: They also wished to set bounty scales to recruit people and to suspend the Guangxi horse-corps tribute for three years to buy oxen.
translations.idiomatic: They also proposed bounty scales for recruitment and a three-year halt to the Guangxi horse tribute so the proceeds could buy oxen.

sentences.zh: 會有訴襄陽屯田之擾者，上欲罷之。

translations.literal: Just then there were complaints about the disturbance of Xiangyang military colonies, and the emperor wished to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Complaints about abuses at Xiangyang's military colonies reached the throne, and the emperor moved to shut them down.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書張闡言：「今日荊襄屯田之害，以其無耕田之民而課之遊民，遊民不足而強之百姓，於是百姓舍己熟田而耕官生田，或遠數百里征呼以來，或名雙丁而役其強壯，老稚無養，一方騷然，罷之誠是也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Kai said: "Today's harm in Jing-Xiang military colonies lies in having no farming people yet levying on vagrants; when vagrants were insufficient they forced commoners—whereupon commoners abandoned their own ripe fields to farm the state's raw land, or were summoned from hundreds of li away, or under the name of two adult males only the strong were impressed while old and young went unsupported; one region was in uproar—abolition is indeed right.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Kai argued: "The trouble at Jing-Xiang colonies is that men with no land to farm are taxed while vagrants are pressed into service; when vagrants ran short, commoners were dragooned—leaving their own ripe fields to work raw government soil, hauled in from hundreds of li away, or taxed as two-adult households while only the strong were taken and the old and young left destitute. The region was in turmoil, and abolition is justified.

sentences.zh: 然自去歲以來，置耕牛農器，修長、木二渠，費已十餘萬，一旦舉而棄之，則荊襄之地終不可耕也。

translations.literal: Yet since last year oxen and farm tools have been provided and the Long and Wood canals repaired, at a cost already of more than one hundred thousand; if all is abandoned at once, the lands of Jing-Xiang will never be cultivable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since last year more than one hundred thousand has been spent on oxen, tools, and the Long and Wood canals; to throw that away now would be to abandon Jing-Xiang cultivation for good.

sentences.zh: 比見兩淮歸正之民，動以萬計，官不能續食，則老弱饑死，強者轉而之他。

translations.literal: Recently one sees people returning to allegiance on the Two Huai in numbers of tens of thousands; if the state cannot continue feeding them, the old and weak starve while the strong drift elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees returning to the Two Huai now number tens of thousands; if the state cannot keep feeding them, the old and weak starve and the strong wander off.

sentences.zh: 若使之就耕荊襄之田，非惟可免流離，抑使中原之民聞之，知朝廷有以處我，率皆繈負而至矣。

translations.literal: If they were made to farm the fields of Jing-Xiang, not only would wandering be avoided, but people of the Central Plain hearing of it would know the court had a place for them and would all come carrying infants on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Set them to farming Jing-Xiang and you not only halt the wandering—you show people of the Central Plain that the court has a place for them, and they will come in swarms with infants on their backs.

sentences.zh: 異時墾辟既廣，取其餘以輸官，實為兩便。

translations.literal: When reclamation has grown broad in time, taking the surplus for delivery to the state would truly be doubly convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Once reclamation widens, the surplus delivered to the state would serve both people and treasury.

sentences.zh: 」詔除見耕者依舊，餘令虞允文同王玨措置。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that what was already under cultivation continue as before; the remainder was entrusted to Yu Yunwen together with Wang Jue to organize.
translations.idiomatic: An edict kept fields already under cultivation as they were and assigned the rest to Yu Yunwen and Wang Jue.

sentences.zh: 二年，江、淮都督府參讚陳俊卿言：「欲以不披帶人，擇官荒田，標旗立砦，多買牛犁，縱耕其中，官不收租，人自樂從。

translations.literal: In the second year, Chen Junqing, staff officer of the Jiang-Huai Chief Council, said: "I wish to use men not bearing arms, choose abandoned government fields, mark flags and erect stockades, buy many oxen and plows, and let them farm freely within; the state collects no rent and people will gladly follow.
translations.idiomatic: In 1164 Chen Junqing of the Jiang-Huai Chief Council proposed using unarmed men on abandoned government land, marking out stockades, buying oxen and plows in quantity, and letting them farm rent-free so that people would come willingly.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，墾田必多，穀必賤。

translations.literal: After several years reclaimed fields will surely be many and grain surely cheap.
translations.idiomatic: In a few years reclaimed acreage would swell and grain would cheapen.

sentences.zh: 所在有屯，則村落無盜賊之憂；

translations.literal: Wherever there are colonies, villages need not fear bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Colonies scattered across the land would spare villages the fear of bandits;

sentences.zh: 軍食既足，則饋餉無轉運之勞。

translations.literal: once military food is sufficient, provisioning need not suffer the labor of transport.
translations.idiomatic: and once army rations were secure, the burden of long supply lines would lift.

sentences.zh: 此誠經久守淮之策。

translations.literal: This is truly a long-term strategy for holding the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: That, he said, was the lasting way to hold the Huai line.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年三月，四川宣撫使鄭剛中撥軍耕種，以歲收租米對減成都路對糴米一十二萬石贍軍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Qiandao, Sichuan Pacification Commissioner Zheng Gangzhong assigned troops to farm, offsetting twelve thousand shi of harmonized-purchase rice on the Chengdu route against the annual rent rice to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1169 Sichuan pacification commissioner Zheng Gangzhong put troops to the plow, applying the annual rent harvest against twelve thousand shi of Chengdu-route harmonized-purchase rice for army rations.

sentences.zh: 然兵民雜處村疃，為擾百端；

translations.literal: Yet soldiers and civilians mixed in villages and hamlets, giving rise to disturbances in every form;
translations.idiomatic: But soldiers and civilians mingled in every hamlet, and trouble sprouted on every side;

sentences.zh: 又數百里外差民保甲教耕，有二、三年不代者，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: and civilians from community-defense units hundreds of li away were dispatched to teach farming, some not replaced for two or three years—the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: and community-defense peasants were drafted from hundreds of li away to teach farming, some not relieved for two or three years, to the people's great distress.

sentences.zh: 知興元府晁公武欲以三年所收最高一年為額，等第均數召佃，放兵及保甲以護邊。
