translations.literal: Chao Gongwu, prefect of Xingyuan, wished to take the highest year's harvest of the past three years as the quota, call tenants by graded equal shares, and release troops and community-defense units to guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Gongwu, prefect of Xingyuan, proposed fixing the quota at the best of three years' harvests, recruiting tenants by graded shares, and freeing troops and militia for border defense.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔鎮江都統司及武鋒軍三處屯田兵並拘收入隊教閱。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict ordered military-colony troops of the Zhenjiang Command, the Wufeng Army, and three other sites all registered and absorbed into their units for drill and inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict recalled military-colony troops at the Zhenjiang command, the Wufeng Army, and three other posts to their units for drill.

sentences.zh: 六年，罷和、揚州屯田。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, military colonies at He and Yangzhou were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1170 military colonies at Hezhou and Yangzhou were abolished.

sentences.zh: 八年，復罷廬州兵屯田。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, military colonies of troops at Luzhou were again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1172 Luzhou's troop colonies were abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十年，鄂州、江陵府駐紮副都統製郭杲言：「襄陽屯田，興置二十餘年，未能大有益於邊計。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chunxi, Guo Gao, deputy overall commander stationed at Ezhou and Jiangling, said: "Xiangyang military colonies, established for more than twenty years, have not greatly benefited frontier finance.
translations.idiomatic: In 1183 Guo Gao, deputy overall commander at Ezhou and Jiangling, reported: "Xiangyang's military colonies, running more than twenty years, have scarcely helped frontier finance.

sentences.zh: 非田之不良，蓋人力有所未至。

translations.literal: It is not that the fields are poor—rather, human effort has not yet reached its limit.
translations.idiomatic: The soil is not to blame—effort has simply fallen short.

sentences.zh: 今邊陲無事，正宜修舉，為實邊之計。

translations.literal: Now the border is quiet; it is exactly the time to restore and promote them as a plan to solidify the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: With the frontier at peace, he urged renewal as the way to make the border truly secure.

sentences.zh: 本司有荒熟田七百五十頃，乞降錢三萬緡，收買耕牛農具，便可施功。

translations.literal: This command has seven hundred fifty qing of fallow and mature fields; I beg that thirty thousand strings of cash be granted to purchase plow oxen and farm tools so work can begin at once.
translations.idiomatic: His command held seven hundred fifty qing of idle and half-worked land; he asked for thirty thousand strings to buy oxen and tools and begin at once.

sentences.zh: 如將來更有餘力，可括荒田接續開墾。

translations.literal: If in future there is further capacity, wasteland may be registered and opened in succession.
translations.idiomatic: If capacity allowed later, more wasteland could be registered and opened in turn.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，知和州劉煒以剩田募民充萬弩手分耕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi, Liu Wei, prefect of Hezhou, used surplus fields to recruit civilians as ten-thousand crossbowmen to farm in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1190 Liu Wei, prefect of Hezhou, used surplus land to recruit civilians as ten-thousand crossbowmen farming in rotation.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年，以京西屯田募人耕種。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading, Jingxi military colonies recruited people to farm.
translations.idiomatic: In 1214 Jingxi military colonies recruited farmers.

sentences.zh: 十三年，四川宣撫安丙、總領任處厚言：「紹興十五年，諸州共墾田二千六百五十餘頃，夏秋輸租米一十四萬一千餘石，餉所屯將兵，罷民和糴，為利可謂博矣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Sichuan Pacification Commissioner An Bing and overall fiscal commissioner Ren Chuhou said: "In the fifteenth year of Shaoxing, the various prefectures together reclaimed more than two thousand six hundred fifty qing; in summer and autumn they paid rent rice of more than one hundred forty-one thousand shi, supplying the garrisoned troops stationed there, abolishing harmonized civilian purchase—the profit can be called vast.
translations.idiomatic: In 1220 Sichuan pacification commissioner An Bing and fiscal commissioner Ren Chuhou reported: "In 1145 the prefectures together reclaimed more than twenty-six hundred fifty qing, paid one hundred forty-one thousand shi of rent rice in summer and autumn, fed the garrisoned troops, and ended harmonized civilian purchase—the gain was enormous.

sentences.zh: 乾道四年以後，屯兵歸軍教閱，而營田付諸州募佃，遂致租利陷失，驕將豪民乘時占據，其弊不可概舉。

translations.literal: After the fourth year of Qiandao, colony troops returned to their armies for drill and inspection while garrison farms were turned over to the prefectures for tenant recruitment, whereupon rent profits were lost and arrogant generals and powerful commoners seized the moment to occupy land—the abuses cannot be summarized.
translations.idiomatic: After 1168 colony troops went back to drill while garrison lands were leased by the prefectures; rent revenue collapsed, arrogant generals and local strongmen grabbed what they could, and the abuses are too many to list.

sentences.zh: 今豪強移徙，田土荒閑，正當拘種之秋，合自總領所與宣撫司措置。

translations.literal: Now the powerful have moved away and the fields lie idle; it is exactly the season for registered planting—it should jointly be arranged by the Overall Fiscal Office and the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Now the bullies have gone and the fields lie fallow; this is the season to put them under cultivation again, they said, and the fiscal and pacification offices should jointly take charge.

sentences.zh: 其逃絕之田，關內外亦多有之，為數不資，其利不在營田之下，乞並括之。

translations.literal: As for abandoned fields, there are also many within and beyond the passes, numbering not a few; their profit is not below that of garrison farms—I beg that they too be registered.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoned fields within and beyond the passes are likewise numerous and no less profitable than garrison farms—they asked that those be registered too.

sentences.zh: 」初，玠守蜀，以軍儲不繼，治褒城堰為屯田，民不以為便。

translations.literal: Initially, when Jie guarded Shu, because military stores did not continue, he restored the Bao city weir as military colonies, and the people did not regard it as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Jie first held Shu, military stores ran short and he turned the Bao city weir into colonies; the people found it anything but convenient.

sentences.zh: 因漕臣郭大中言，約中其數，使民自耕。

translations.literal: On the word of transport official Guo Dazhong, the quota was reduced to the middle figure and the people were allowed to farm for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At transport official Guo Dazhong's urging, the levy was cut to a median figure and the people were left to farm on their own.

sentences.zh: 民皆歸業，而歲入多於屯田。

translations.literal: The people all returned to their occupations, and annual revenue exceeded that from garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: Every household went back to its trade, and yearly income from the fields surpassed what the military colonies had yielded.

sentences.zh: 端平元年八月，以臣僚言，屯五萬人於淮之南北，且田且守，置屯田判官一員經紀其事，暇則教以騎射。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Duanping, on the advice of court officials, fifty thousand men were encamped north and south of the Huai River to farm while guarding; one garrison-farming intendant was appointed to manage the matter, and in leisure hours they were taught mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: In August of Duanping 1, following memorials from the bureaucracy, the court settled fifty thousand troops on both banks of the Huai to cultivate land and hold the line. A special intendant supervised the scheme, drilling the men in horsemanship and archery whenever they were off duty.

sentences.zh: 初弛田租三年，又三年則取其半。

translations.literal: At first field rents were remitted for three years; after another three years half was collected.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax was waived entirely for the first three years; in the next three, only half was levied.

sentences.zh: 十月，知大寧監邵潛言：「昔鄭剛中嘗於蜀之關隘雜兵民屯田，歲收粟二十餘萬石。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Shao Qian, supervisor of the Daining Directorate, said: "Formerly Zheng Gangzhong once mixed soldiers and civilians to farm garrison fields at the passes of Shu, collecting more than two hundred thousand shi of grain annually.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Shao Qian, director of the Daining office, memorialized: "Zheng Gangzhong had once intermingled troops and commoners for frontier farming at the mountain passes of Shu, harvesting over two hundred thousand shi of grain each year.

sentences.zh: 是後屯田之利既廢，糧運之費益增，宜詔帥臣縱兵民耕之，所收之粟計直以償之，則總所無轉輸之苦，邊關有儲峙之豐，戰有餘勇，守有餘備矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter the benefits of garrison farming were abandoned, and the costs of grain transport steadily increased; it would be fitting to issue an edict allowing frontier commanders to let soldiers and people cultivate, compensating them at calculated value for grain collected—then the general supply office would be free of transport hardship, the border would have ample stored provisions, and there would be surplus strength for battle and surplus stores for defense."
translations.idiomatic: Since then that system had lapsed and freight costs had climbed. He urged the court to let frontier commanders put soldiers and civilians back on the land and pay fair value for the harvest, sparing the supply bureau endless convoys, filling the passes with stores, and leaving campaigns and garrisons with grain to spare."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙四年，令流民於邊江七十里內分田以耕，遇警則用以守江；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaxi, displaced people were ordered within seventy li of the river frontier to receive allotments of land to farm; when alarms arose they were used to defend the river.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 4, refugees along the Yangtze frontier were given plots to till within seventy li of the banks; at the first alarm they were to man the river line.

sentences.zh: 於邊城三、五十里內亦分田以耕，遇警則用以守城；

translations.literal: Within thirty or fifty li of frontier cities they likewise received divided fields to farm; when alarms arose they were used to defend the cities.
translations.idiomatic: Similar allotments were made thirty to fifty li outside border towns, with the same duty to fall in for urban defense when danger threatened.

sentences.zh: 在砦者則耕四野之田，而用以守砦。

translations.literal: Those in stockades then farmed fields in the surrounding countryside and were used to defend the stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Men stationed in fortified camps worked the open fields around them and rallied to hold those camps.

sentences.zh: 田在官者免其租，在民者以所收十之一二歸其主，俟三年事定則各還元業。

translations.literal: Land belonging to the state was exempt from rent; on private land one or two tenths of the harvest went back to the owner, and after three years, when matters were settled, each returned to his original occupation.
translations.idiomatic: State land was rent-free; on private plots, only ten or twenty percent of the crop went to the original owner. After three years of calm, every man was to return to his former livelihood.

sentences.zh: 咸淳三年，詔曰：「淮、蜀、湖、襄之民所種屯田，既困重額，又困苛取，流離之餘，口體不充，及遇水旱，收租不及，而催輸急於星火，民何以堪！

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianchun, an edict said: "The people of Huai, Shu, Hu, and Xiang who farm garrison fields are already burdened by heavy quotas and harsh exactions; after being scattered and displaced, they cannot fill mouth and body, and when flood or drought comes they cannot meet harvest quotas, yet collection is pressed faster than sparks—how can the people bear it!
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianchun an imperial edict declared: "Peasants farming military colonies in the Huai, Shu, Hunan, and Xiang regions are crushed between punitive quotas and corrupt levies. Already uprooted and half-starved, they cannot meet the tax when flood or drought strikes—yet collectors descend like wildfire. How can the people bear it!

sentences.zh: 其日前舊欠並除之，復催者以違制論。」

translations.literal: All past arrears to date are to be remitted; those who again press for collection shall be treated as violating regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Every outstanding debt is cancelled, and any official who duns the people again will be prosecuted for violating regulations."

sentences.zh: 常平、義倉，漢、隋利民之良法，常平以平穀價，義倉以備凶災。

translations.literal: Ever-Normal Granaries and Charity Granaries were fine methods of the Han and Sui for benefiting the people: Ever-Normal to stabilize grain prices, Charity Granaries to prepare against famine and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Normal and Charity Granary systems were two exemplary Han and Sui policies for the common good—the first to even out grain prices, the second to stockpile against famine.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，又置惠民倉，以雜配錢分數折粟貯之，歲歉，減價出以惠民。

translations.literal: In the Xiande reign of Zhou, Benefiting-the-People granaries were also established; miscellaneous apportioned money was converted in fixed shares to stored grain, and in lean years it was sold at reduced price to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou Xiande, the court added People's Relief granaries, turning assorted surcharge payments into stored grain to be sold cheaply in bad harvest years.

sentences.zh: 宋兼存其法焉。

translations.literal: The Song likewise retained these methods together.
translations.idiomatic: The Song preserved all three institutions.

sentences.zh: 太祖承五季之亂，海內多事，義倉浸廢。

translations.literal: Taizu inherited the chaos of the Five Dynasties; within the seas there were many disturbances, and Charity Granaries gradually fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu seized power amid the wreckage of the Five Dynasties, civil turmoil left the Charity Granaries moribund.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，詔諸州於各縣置義倉，歲輸二稅，石別收一斗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, an edict ordered each prefecture to establish Charity Granaries in every county; on the two annual tax deliveries, one dou was collected per shi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande, the throne mandated a Charity Granary in every county, funded by a one-dou levy on each shi of the twice-yearly land tax.

sentences.zh: 民饑欲貸充種食者，縣具籍申州，州長吏即計口貸訖，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: When hungry people wished loans for seed grain, the county compiled registers and reported to the prefecture; the prefectural chief official then loaned according to mouths counted, and only afterward reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Starving farmers who needed seed grain would be registered by the county, the prefect would lend grain by headcount on the spot, and only then notify the capital.

sentences.zh: 其後以輸送煩勞，罷之。

translations.literal: Later, because transport was troublesome and laborious, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme was later scrapped as too burdensome to supply.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，京畿大穰，分遣使臣於四城門置場，增價以糴，虛近倉貯之，命曰常平，歲饑即下其直予民。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, the capital region had a great harvest; emissaries were dispatched to set up markets at the four city gates, buying at increased price and storing in nearby empty granaries, named Ever-Normal; in famine years the standard price was lowered to give to the people.
translations.idiomatic: After a bumper harvest around the capital in Chunhua 3, agents opened purchase stations at all four gates, paying above market to buy grain for nearby empty stores—the Ever-Normal Granaries. In famine years grain was sold back to the people at the original price.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，庫部員外郎成肅請福建增置惠民倉，因詔諸路申淳化惠民之制。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, Cheng Su, outer-section member of the treasury bureau, requested that Fujian add Benefiting-the-People granaries; consequently an edict ordered all circuits to report on the Chunhua system for benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping, Treasury official Cheng Su persuaded the court to expand People's Relief granaries in Fujian, prompting an empire-wide review of the Chunhua relief model.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，言事者請於京東西、河北、河東、陝西、江南、淮南、兩浙皆立常平倉，計戶口多寡，量留上供錢自二三千貫至一二萬貫，令轉運使每州擇清幹官主之，領於司農寺，三司無輒移用。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, memorialists requested Ever-Normal granaries in Hebei East and West, Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, Jiangnan, Huainan, and the two Zhe circuits; according to population more or less, two to three thousand to ten or twenty thousand strings of submitted tribute money were retained; transport commissioners in each prefecture were to choose upright officials to preside, under the Ministry of Revenue, and the Three Departments were not to requisition at will.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde 3 brought a memorial to establish Ever-Normal stores across Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, Jiangnan, Huainan, and both Zhes. Each prefecture would keep two or three thousand to as many as ten or twenty thousand strings of tribute funds, proportioned to household counts. Transport commissioners were to appoint honest officers to manage them under the Ministry of Revenue, with the Three Departments forbidden to raid the funds.

sentences.zh: 歲夏秋視市價量增以糴，糶減價亦如之，所減不得過本錢。

translations.literal: Each summer and autumn, according to market price grain was bought at measured increase; sales at reduced price likewise, and the reduction might not exceed the original capital.
translations.idiomatic: Each summer and autumn officials bought grain above market when prices fell and sold below market when they rose, never discounting below the original purchase cost.

sentences.zh: 而沿邊州郡不置。

translations.literal: But border prefectures and commanderies were not to establish them.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier districts were exempt.

sentences.zh: 詔三司集議，請如所奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Departments to convene for deliberation; the request was approved as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments deliberated and recommended adoption as proposed.

sentences.zh: 於是增置司農官吏，創廨舍，藏籍帳，度支別置常平案。

translations.literal: Thereupon agricultural officials were added, office buildings created, ledgers stored, and the expenditure bureau separately established an Ever-Normal section.
translations.idiomatic: New Ministry of Revenue staff, offices, and ledgers followed, and the Expenditure Bureau created a dedicated Ever-Normal desk.

sentences.zh: 大率萬戶歲糴萬石，戶雖多，止五萬石。

translations.literal: Generally ten thousand households yearly purchased ten thousand shi; though households were many, the ceiling was fifty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The rule of thumb was ten thousand shi per ten thousand households, capped at fifty thousand shi no matter how large the county.

sentences.zh: 三年以上不糶，即回充糧廩，易以新粟。

translations.literal: If not sold out within three years or more, it was returned to fill the commissary and exchanged for new grain.
translations.idiomatic: Grain unsold after three years was rotated into military stores and replaced with fresh stock.

sentences.zh: 災傷州郡糴粟，鬥毋過百錢。

translations.literal: In disaster-stricken prefectures and commanderies purchasing grain, per dou might not exceed one hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: In disaster counties purchase price was capped at one hundred cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 後又詔當職官於元約數外增糴及一倍已上者，並與理為勞績。

translations.literal: Later an edict further ordered that incumbent officials who increased purchases beyond the original quota by one fold or more would all have it counted as merit in service.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who doubled their purchase quotas would have the excess credited as meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，荊湖、川峽、廣南皆增置常平倉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi, Jinghu, Chuanxia, and Guangnan all added Ever-Normal granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi 4 extended Ever-Normal stores to Jinghu, Sichuan gorges, and Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 五年，諸路總糴數十八萬三千餘斛，糶二十四萬三千餘斛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the total purchases of all circuits were one hundred eighty-three thousand-odd hu, and sales two hundred forty-three thousand-odd hu.
translations.idiomatic: By year five circuits had bought 183,000 hu and sold 243,000 hu.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，淮南轉運副使吳遵路言：「本路丁口百五十萬，而常平錢粟才四十餘萬，歲饑不足以救恤。

translations.literal: In the Jingyou era, Wu Zunlu, vice transport commissioner of Huainan, said: "This circuit has one million five hundred thousand adult mouths, yet Ever-Normal money and grain are only four hundred thousand-odd; in famine years it is insufficient for relief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou era, Huainan vice transport commissioner Wu Zunlu said: "This circuit has one million five hundred thousand adult mouths, yet Ever-Normal money and grain total only four hundred thousand-odd; in famine years that is insufficient for relief.

sentences.zh: 願自經畫增為二百萬，他毋得移用。

translations.literal: I wish to plan and increase it to two million myself; none other may requisition it."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to raise the reserve to two million myself; none other may divert it."

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 後又詔：天下常平錢粟，三司轉運司皆毋得移用。

translations.literal: Later an edict further ordered: Ever-Normal money and grain throughout the realm—neither the Three Departments nor transport commissions might requisition.
translations.idiomatic: A later edict barred both the Three Departments and transport offices from touching Ever-Normal reserves anywhere in the empire.

sentences.zh: 不數年間，常平積有餘而兵食不足，乃命司農寺出常平錢百萬緡助三司給軍費。

translations.literal: Within a few years Ever-Normal accumulations had surplus while military provisions were insufficient; the Ministry of Revenue was then ordered to disburse one million strings of Ever-Normal money to aid the Three Departments in supplying army expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Within years the Ever-Normal coffers swelled even as army rations ran short, so the court released one million strings from the granary funds to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 久之，移用數多，而蓄藏無幾矣。

translations.literal: After long time, requisitions were many, and stored reserves were nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated raids soon drained the reserves.

sentences.zh: 自景祐初畿內饑，詔出常平粟貸中下戶，戶一斛。

translations.literal: From the famine in the capital region at the start of Jingyou, an edict ordered Ever-Normal grain lent to middle and lower households, one hu per household.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region famished early in Jingyou, middle and lower households each received one hu on loan from the Ever-Normal stores.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，發京西常平粟振貧民，而聚斂者或增舊價糶粟，欲以市恩；

translations.literal: In the Qingli era, Ever-Normal grain of western capital was released to relieve the poor, but some tax-gatherers sold grain at increased old price, wishing to buy favor.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingli western-capital grain was opened for the poor, yet some venal officials marked up the sale price to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 皇祐三年，詔誡之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangyou, an edict admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyou 3 brought an imperial rebuke.

sentences.zh: 淮南、兩浙體量安撫陳升之等言：「災傷州軍乞糶常平倉粟，令於元價上量添十文、十五文，殊非恤民之意。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng-zhi and others, pacification commissioners surveying Huainan and the two Zhes, said: "Disaster-stricken prefectures and armies requesting to sell Ever-Normal grain were ordered to add ten or fifteen cash on the original price—utterly contrary to the intent of cherishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioners Chen Sheng-zhi and others said: "Disaster-stricken prefectures and armies seeking to sell Ever-Normal grain were told to add ten or fifteen cash above the purchase price—utterly contrary to the intent of cherishing the people.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔止於元糴價出糶。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon ordered sales only at the original purchase price."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered sales only at the original purchase price."

sentences.zh: 五年，詔曰：「比者湖北歲儉，發常平以濟饑者，如聞司農寺復督取，豈朝廷振恤意哉？

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict said: "Recently Hubei had a lean year and Ever-Normal was released to aid the hungry; we hear the Ministry of Revenue again pressed for repayment—is this the court's intent to relieve and succor?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict said: "Recently Hubei had a lean year and Ever-Normal grain was released to aid the hungry; we hear the Ministry of Revenue again pressed for repayment—is this the court's intent to relieve and succor?

sentences.zh: 其悉除之。」

translations.literal: All such debts are completely remitted."
translations.idiomatic: All such debts are completely remitted."

sentences.zh: 明道二年，詔議復義倉，不果。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao, an edict ordered deliberation on restoring Charity Granaries; it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdao 2 revived debate over Charity Granaries, but nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，集賢校理王琪請復置：「令五等已上戶，隨夏秋二稅，二斗別輸一升，水旱減稅則免輸。

translations.literal: In the Jingyou era, Wang Qi, collator in the Hanlin Academy, requested restoration: "Order households of the fifth rank and above, with the summer and autumn two taxes, for every two dou separately submit one sheng; when water and drought reduce taxes, submission is exempted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou era, Hanlin collator Wang Qi proposed reviving Charity Granaries: "Let households of the fifth rank and above, with the summer and autumn two taxes, for every two dou separately submit one sheng; when water and drought reduce taxes, submission is exempted.

sentences.zh: 州縣擇便地置倉貯之，領於轉運使。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties would choose convenient sites to establish granaries for storage, supervised by transport commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Counties would site stores at convenient locations under transport commissioners.

sentences.zh: 計以一中郡正稅歲入十萬石，則義倉可得五千石，推而廣之，則利博矣。

translations.literal: Calculating by a medium commandery whose regular tax yearly intake is one hundred thousand shi, Charity Granaries could obtain five thousand shi; extended broadly, the benefit would be vast.
translations.idiomatic: A typical county yielding one hundred thousand shi could stock five thousand—a model that scaled empire-wide would be transformative.

sentences.zh: 明道中，饑歉，國家欲盡貸饑民則軍食不足，故民有流轉之患。

translations.literal: In the Mingdao era, famine and scarcity: if the state wished to lend fully to hungry people then military provisions were insufficient, so the people had the affliction of wandering displacement.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingdao famine years the state could not feed both the army and the starving, and refugees filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 是時，兼並之家出粟數千石則補吏，是豈以官爵為輕歟？

translations.literal: At that time, consolidating households that contributed several thousand shi of grain were appointed minor officials—is it that they held office and rank lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy landlords who donated thousands of shi won petty office—surely they did not scorn rank?

sentences.zh: 特愛民濟物，不獲已為之爾。

translations.literal: They simply loved the people and aided things; they did it because they could not do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: They acted from genuine concern for the afflicted, having no other choice.

sentences.zh: 且兼並之家占田常廣，則義倉所入常多；

translations.literal: Moreover, consolidating households usually occupied broad land, so Charity Granary intake was usually large;
translations.idiomatic: Large landowners held the most fields and would contribute the most;

sentences.zh: 中下之家占田常狹，則義倉所入常少。

translations.literal: Middle and lower households usually occupied narrow land, so Charity Granary intake was usually small.
translations.idiomatic: modest farmers held less and would pay less.

sentences.zh: 及水旱振濟，則兼並之家未必待此而濟，中下之民實先受其賜矣。

translations.literal: When flood and drought relief was distributed, consolidating households might not need this to survive, while middle and lower people would truly receive the benefit first.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in disaster the rich needed no relief, while middling and poor families would be saved first.

sentences.zh: 」事下有司會議，議者異同而止。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for departmental joint deliberation; deliberators differed and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the ministries, where divided counsel killed it.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，琪復上其議，仁宗納之，命天下立義倉，詔上三等戶輸粟，已而復罷。

translations.literal: At the start of Qingli, Qi again submitted his proposal; Renzong accepted it and ordered Charity Granaries established throughout the realm, decreeing upper three ranks to submit grain; soon after it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingli Wang Qi pressed again; Renzong ordered Charity Granaries empire-wide with levies on the top three household ranks—then cancelled the scheme.

sentences.zh: 其後賈黯又言：「今天下無事，年穀豐熟，民人安樂，父子相保。

translations.literal: Thereafter Jia An also said: "Today the realm is without incident, year-grain abundantly ripe, people peaceful and joyous, fathers and sons mutually preserving one another.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jia An also said: "Today the realm is without incident, the harvest is abundant, the people are peaceful and joyous, and fathers and sons keep one another safe.

sentences.zh: 一遇水旱，則流離死亡，捐棄道路，發倉廩振之則糧不給，課粟富人則力不贍，轉輸千里則不及事，移民就粟則遠近交困。

translations.literal: Once flood or drought strikes, then wandering, death, and abandonment on the roads; opening granaries to relieve gives insufficient grain, levying grain from the rich gives insufficient strength, transporting a thousand li cannot meet the emergency, moving people toward grain makes near and far mutually distressed.
translations.idiomatic: One drought turned abundance to corpses on the highways; state granaries could not stretch, levies on the wealthy could not suffice, grain convoyed a thousand li arrived too late, and resettling the hungry only spread misery.

sentences.zh: 朝廷之臣，郡縣之吏，倉卒不知所出，則民饑而死者過半矣。

translations.literal: Court ministers and prefectural and county officials, in haste knowing no way out, then more than half the people would starve and die.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers and magistrates panicked without a plan, half the populace could perish.

sentences.zh: 願放隋制立民社義倉，詔天下州軍遇年穀豐登，立法勸課蓄積，以備凶災。

translations.literal: I wish to follow the Sui system and establish people's commune Charity Granaries; decree that throughout the realm, wherever year-grain is abundant, laws encourage accumulation to prepare against famine and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He urged restoring Sui-style communal Charity Granaries, with laws encouraging every prosperous prefecture to save against calamity.

sentences.zh: 此所謂『樂歲粒米狼戾，多取之而不為虐』者也，況取之以為民耶？

translations.literal: This is what is called 'In good years grain lies about in abundance—taking more is not cruelty'; moreover, is it not taking for the people's sake?
translations.idiomatic: As Mencius said, abundance permits levy without cruelty—and here the levy would serve the people themselves.

sentences.zh: 」下其說諸路以度可否，以為可行才四路，餘或謂賦稅之外兩重供輸，或謂恐招盜賊，或謂已有常平足以振給，或謂置倉煩擾。

translations.literal: His proposal was sent to circuits to gauge feasibility; only four circuits deemed it workable; others said beyond tax another double submission, or feared attracting robbers, or said existing Ever-Normal sufficed for relief, or said establishing granaries would be troublesome.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was sent to the circuits to gauge feasibility; only four deemed it workable; others cited double taxation, fear of bandits, faith in Ever-Normal stores, or administrative burden.

sentences.zh: 於是黯復上奏曰：「臣嘗判尚書刑部，見天下歲斷死刑多至四千餘人，其間盜賊率十六七，蓋愚民迫於饑寒，因之水旱，枉陷重辟。

translations.literal: Thereupon An again memorialized: "I once served as judge of the Ministry of Justice and saw annual death sentences nationwide often reach more than four thousand; of these robbers comprised sixteen or seventeen in ten—ignorant people pressed by hunger and cold, owing to flood and drought, wrongly fallen into capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jia An again memorialized: "I once served as judge of the Ministry of Justice and saw annual death sentences nationwide often reach more than four thousand; of these robbers comprised sixteen or seventeen in ten—ignorant people pressed by hunger and cold, owing to flood and drought, wrongly fallen into capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 故臣請復民社義倉，以備凶歲。

translations.literal: Therefore I request restoration of people's commune Charity Granaries to prepare for bad years.
translations.idiomatic: Charity Granaries, he insisted, were the only hedge against such years.

sentences.zh: 今諸路所陳，類皆妄議。

translations.literal: Now what circuits present are mostly reckless talk.
translations.idiomatic: The objections from the circuits were mostly spurious.

sentences.zh: 若謂賦稅之外兩重供輸，則義倉之意，乃教民儲積以備水旱，官為立法，非以自利，行之既久，民必樂輸。

translations.literal: If one says beyond tax a double submission, then the intent of Charity Granaries is to teach people to accumulate against flood and drought; the state establishes laws, not for self-profit; practiced long, the people will surely gladly submit.
translations.idiomatic: On double taxation: Charity Granaries teach self-reliance against disaster—public law for public good. Given time, people would contribute willingly.

sentences.zh: 若謂恐招盜賊，盜賊利在輕貨，不在粟麥，今鄉村富室有貯粟數萬石者，不聞有劫掠之虞。

translations.literal: If one says fear of attracting robbers—robbers profit from light goods, not grain and wheat; today rich village households store tens of thousands of shi without report of pillaging.
translations.idiomatic: On bandits: thieves prefer gold to grain; wealthy villages store tens of thousands of shi without incident.

sentences.zh: 且盜賊之起，本由貧困。

translations.literal: Moreover, robbers arise fundamentally from poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry itself springs from want.

sentences.zh: 臣建此議，欲使民有貯積，雖遇水旱，不憂乏食，則人人自愛而重犯法，此正消除盜賊之原也。

translations.literal: My proposal aims to let people have stores; though flood and drought come, without fear of lacking food, then every person will cherish himself and value not violating law—this is precisely eliminating the root of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Full barns would let men live without crime—the true cure for banditry.

sentences.zh: 若謂有常平足以振給，則常平之設，蓋以準平穀價，使無甚貴甚賤之傷。

translations.literal: If one says Ever-Normal suffices for relief—Ever-Normal's establishment was basically to standardize and level grain prices, so there would be no injury of too dear or too cheap.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-Normal granaries were meant to stabilize prices, not sustain famine relief.

sentences.zh: 或遇凶饑，發以振救，既已失其本意，而費又出公帑，今國用頗乏，所蓄不厚。

translations.literal: Or when famine strikes, releasing for relief already loses the original intent, and expense comes from the public treasury; now state use is quite deficient, stored reserves not thick.
translations.idiomatic: Using them for relief perverts their purpose, drains the treasury, and reserves are already thin.

sentences.zh: 近歲非無常平，小有水旱，輒流離餓莩，起為盜賊，則是常平果不足仰以振給也。

translations.literal: In recent years it was not that there was no Ever-Normal; at slight flood or drought people at once wandered, starved on the roads, and rose as robbers—then Ever-Normal truly cannot be relied on for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Recent minor disasters still produced refugees and bandits—clear proof Ever-Normal stores cannot carry the burden.

sentences.zh: 若謂置倉廩，斂材木，恐有煩擾，則今州縣修治郵傳驛舍，皆斂於民，豈於義倉獨畏煩擾？

translations.literal: If one says establishing granaries and collecting timber and wood may cause trouble—today prefectures and counties repair postal relay stations, all levied from the people; why alone fear trouble for Charity Granaries?
translations.idiomatic: As for administrative burden, the state constantly conscripted labor for post stations—Charity Granaries deserved no special timidity.

sentences.zh: 人情可與樂成，不可與謀始，願自朝廷斷而行之。

translations.literal: Human sentiment can share in completing joy, cannot share in planning the beginning; I wish the court to decide and execute.
translations.idiomatic: People resist new ideas but embrace their fruits—only imperial resolve could break the deadlock.

sentences.zh: 」然當時牽於眾論，終不果行。

translations.literal: Yet at the time constrained by popular opinion, in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the time public opinion prevailed, and in the end the plan was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，詔天下置廣惠倉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, an edict ordered Broad-Benefit granaries established throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 2 mandated Broad Relief granaries nationwide.

sentences.zh: 初，天下沒入戶絕田，官自鬻之。

translations.literal: Initially, escheated land from extinct households throughout the realm was sold by the state itself.
translations.idiomatic: The state had been selling land forfeited by extinct households.

sentences.zh: 樞密使韓琦請留勿鬻，募人耕，收其租別為倉貯之，以給州縣郭內之老幼貧疾不能自存者，領以提點刑獄，歲終具出內之數上之三司。

translations.literal: Privy Councilor Han Qi requested retention without sale, recruiting people to farm, collecting rent separately stored in granaries to supply within prefectures and counties the aged, infirm, poor, and ill unable to support themselves, supervised by judicial-intendent commissioners, year-end reporting disbursements and receipts to the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Privy councilor Han Qi asked to keep such land under cultivation, sequestering rent in new stores to feed the aged, sick, and destitute in county seats under judicial intendants, with annual accounting to the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 戶不滿萬，留田租千石，萬戶倍之，戶二萬留三千石，三萬留四千石，四萬留五千石，五萬留六千石，七萬留八千石，十萬留萬石。

translations.literal: Households not reaching ten thousand—retain one thousand shi field rent; at ten thousand households double it; twenty thousand retain three thousand shi; thirty thousand four thousand shi; forty thousand five thousand shi; fifty thousand six thousand shi; seventy thousand eight thousand shi; one hundred thousand ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Reserves scaled with population: one thousand shi below ten thousand households, doubling at ten thousand, rising to three thousand at twenty thousand, four thousand at thirty thousand, five thousand at forty thousand, six thousand at fifty thousand, eight thousand at seventy thousand, and ten thousand at one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 田有餘，則鬻如舊。

translations.literal: If land had surplus, it was sold as before.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus land was still sold as before.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔改隸司農寺，州選官二人主出納，歲十月遣官驗視，應受米者書名於籍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict changed subordination to the Ministry of Revenue; each prefecture selected two officials to manage receipts and disbursements; each tenth month officials were dispatched to inspect; those due rice had names written in registers.
translations.idiomatic: Year four placed the stores under the Ministry of Revenue, with two local officers managing disbursements, autumn inspections, and registered recipients.

sentences.zh: 自十一月始，三日一給，人米一升，幼者半之，次年二月止。

translations.literal: From the eleventh month distribution began, once every three days one sheng of rice per person, half for the young, stopping the second month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: From November through February each eligible person received one sheng every three days, half rations for children.

sentences.zh: 有餘乃及諸縣，量大小均給之。

translations.literal: If there was surplus it extended to all counties, distributed evenly according to size.
translations.idiomatic: Any surplus went to surrounding counties in proportion to need.

sentences.zh: 其大略如此。

translations.literal: Its general outline was such.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the broad outlines.

sentences.zh: 治平三年，常平入五十萬一千四十八石，出四十七萬一千一百五十七石。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiping, Ever-Normal intake was five hundred one thousand forty-eight shi, outflow four hundred seventy-one thousand one hundred fifty-seven shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiping 3 saw Ever-Normal stores take in 501,048 shi and disburse 471,157 shi.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，製置三司條例司言：「諸路常平、廣惠倉錢穀，略計貫石可及千五百萬以上，斂散未得其宜，故為利未博。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, the Fiscal Reform Bureau said: "Ever-Normal and Broad-Benefit granary money and grain of all circuits, roughly totaling strings and shi could reach more than fifteen million; collection and dispersal did not obtain their proper balance, so benefit was not vast.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xining the Fiscal Reform Bureau said: "Ever-Normal and Broad Relief granary money and grain of all circuits, roughly totaling strings and shi, could reach more than fifteen million; collection and dispersal did not obtain their proper balance, so benefit was not vast.

sentences.zh: 今欲以見在斛斗，遇貴量減市價糶，遇賤量增市價糴，可通融轉運司苗稅及錢斛就便轉易者，亦許兌換。

translations.literal: Now we wish to use grain presently on hand: when dear, sell at measured reduction below market price; when cheap, buy at measured increase above market price; where transport commission seed tax and money-grain can flexibly be exchanged locally, exchange is also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed using existing stores to sell below market when prices rose and buy above market when they fell, with transport offices allowed to swap tax grain and cash as local conditions required.

sentences.zh: 仍以見錢，依陝西青苗錢例，願預借者給之。

translations.literal: Still using cash on hand, following the Shaanxi Green Sprouts money precedent, those wishing advance loans would be given them.
translations.idiomatic: Cash reserves would also fund advance loans on the Shaanxi Green Sprouts model for any farmer who applied.

sentences.zh: 隨稅輸納斛斗，半為夏料，半為秋料，內有請本色或納時價貴願納錢者，皆從其便。

translations.literal: Along with tax, grain in hu and dou was submitted, half as summer installment, half as autumn installment; among them those requesting grain in kind or, when submitting, finding current price dear wishing to submit money—all followed their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Repayment would follow the tax schedule in two halves, summer and autumn, with borrowers free to pay in grain or cash depending on market prices.

sentences.zh: 如遇災傷，許展至次料豐熟日納。

translations.literal: If disaster and injury were encountered, extension to the next installment's day of abundant ripeness for payment was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster victims could defer payment until the next harvest.

sentences.zh: 非惟足以待凶荒之患，民既受貸，則兼並之家不得乘新陳不接以邀倍息。

translations.literal: Not only sufficient to await the affliction of famine and disaster—once the people received loans, consolidating households could not take advantage of the gap between old and new grain to demand doubled interest.
translations.idiomatic: The loans would buffer against famine and keep wealthy landlords from exploiting the lean season with usurious rates.

sentences.zh: 又常平、廣惠之物，收藏積滯，必待年儉物貴然後出糶，所及者不過城市遊手之人。

translations.literal: Moreover, Ever-Normal and Broad-Benefit goods, stored and accumulated stagnant, must wait until lean years when goods are dear before selling—those reached were no more than idle hands in cities.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-Normal and Broad Relief grain sat idle until scarcity drove prices up, benefiting only urban speculators.

sentences.zh: 今通一路有無，貴發賤斂，以廣蓄積，平物價，使農人有以赴時趨事，而兼並不得乘其急。

translations.literal: Now linking surplus and deficit across a circuit, releasing when dear and collecting when cheap, to broaden accumulation and level commodity prices, lets farmers have means to keep season and hurry to tasks, while consolidators cannot take advantage of their urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Circulating reserves across each circuit—selling high, buying low—would stabilize prices, keep farmers working through the seasons, and deny landlords their moment of leverage.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆以為民，而公家無所利其入，是亦先王散惠興利、以為耕斂補助之意也。

translations.literal: All this is for the people's sake, while the public house profits nothing from its intake—this is likewise the intent of the ancient kings in spreading benefit and raising profit, as aid and supplement to plowing and collection.
translations.idiomatic: All of this served the people, not the treasury—true to the sage-kings' ideal of public benefit as support for farming and taxation.

sentences.zh: 欲量諸路錢穀多寡，分遣官提舉，每州選通判幕職官一員，典幹轉移出納，仍先自河北、京東、淮南三路施行，俟有緒推之諸路。

translations.literal: We wish to measure money and grain more or less of all circuits, dispatch officials to oversee, select one assistant prefect or staff official per prefecture to manage transfer of receipts and disbursements, still first implementing from Hebei, Hebei East, and Huainan three circuits; when there is order, extend to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Officials would be dispatched to audit reserves and appoint a deputy in each prefecture to manage transfers, piloting the scheme in Hebei, Hebei East, and Huainan before rolling it out empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 其廣惠倉除量留給老疾貧窮人外，餘並用常平倉轉移法。

translations.literal: Broad-Benefit granaries, aside from measured reserves for the aged, ill, poor, and destitute, would all use the Ever-Normal granary transfer method.
translations.idiomatic: Broad Relief stores would keep only enough for the aged, sick, and poor; the rest would follow Ever-Normal circulation rules.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved."

sentences.zh: 既而條例司又言：「常平、廣惠倉條約，先行於河北、京東、淮南三路，訪問民間多願支貸，乞遍下諸路轉運司施行，當議置提舉官。

translations.literal: Soon after the Regulations Bureau again said: "Ever-Normal and Broad-Benefit granary regulations, first implemented in Hebei, Hebei East, and Huainan three circuits—inquiring among the people many wished to receive loans; we beg to send down to all circuits' transport commissions for implementation, and should deliberate establishing overseeing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the Regulations Bureau again said: "Ever-Normal and Broad Relief granary regulations, first implemented in Hebei, Hebei East, and Huainan three circuits—inquiring among the people many wished to receive loans; we beg to send down to all circuits' transport commissions for implementation, and should deliberate establishing overseeing officials.

sentences.zh: 」時天下常平錢穀見在一千四百萬貫石。

translations.literal: At that time Ever-Normal money and grain currently in store throughout the realm amounted to fourteen million strings and shi."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ever-Normal money and grain currently in store throughout the realm amounted to fourteen million strings and shi."

sentences.zh: 詔諸路各置提舉官二員，以朝官為之，管當一員，京官為之，或共置二員，開封府界一員，凡四十一人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered each circuit to establish two overseeing officials; court officials would fill one post, administrative managers one post, capital officials would fill it—or jointly two posts; the Kaifeng metropolitan district one official; in all forty-one persons.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed two overseers per circuit—one court official and one capital official, or both roles combined—plus one for the Kaifeng metropolitan district, forty-one in all.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗既用王安石為參知政事，安石為帝言天下財利所當開闔斂散者，帝然其說，遂創立製置三司條例司。

translations.literal: At first, after Emperor Shenzong had employed Wang Anshi as Vice Grand Councilor, Anshi told the emperor about what under heaven's finances and profit ought to be opened, closed, gathered, and dispersed; the emperor assented to his doctrine, and thereupon established the Fiscal Reform Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenzong's reign, after making Wang Anshi vice grand councilor, the emperor accepted Wang's argument that the state must actively manage the flow of national wealth, and established the Fiscal Reform Bureau.

sentences.zh: 安石因請以著作佐郎編校集賢書箱呂惠卿為製置司檢詳文字，自是專一講求立為新製，欲行青苗之法。

translations.literal: Anshi thereupon requested that Editorial Assistant for Collation of the Hall of Assembled Talents Lü Huiqing be made the bureau's text examiner; from this, exclusively pursuing establishment of new institutions, he wished to implement the Green Sprouts law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang then appointed Lü Huiqing as text examiner for the bureau and focused on drafting new institutions, above all the Green Sprouts loan program.

sentences.zh: 蘇轍自大名推官上書，召對，亦除條例司檢詳文字。

translations.literal: Su Zhe, from his position as legal officer at Daming, submitted a memorial, was summoned for audience, and was also appointed Regulations Bureau text examiner.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe, a legal officer at Daming, submitted a memorial, was summoned to court, and likewise joined the bureau as text examiner.

sentences.zh: 安石出青苗法示之，轍曰：「以錢貸民，使出息二分，本非為利。

translations.literal: Anshi produced the Green Sprouts law and showed it to him; Zhe said: "Lending money to the people and making them pay two-fen interest was originally not for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang showed Su the Green Sprouts draft. Su said, "Lending cash to farmers at two percent interest was never meant to be a profit scheme.

sentences.zh: 然出納之際，吏緣為奸，雖有法不能禁；

translations.literal: Yet at the junctures of disbursement and receipt, clerks seized the opportunity for corruption; though there were laws, they could not be forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: But at every point of disbursement and collection clerks would find ways to cheat, and no law could stop them;

sentences.zh: 錢入民手，雖良民不免非理費用；

translations.literal: once money entered the people's hands, even good commoners could not avoid unreasonable spending;
translations.idiomatic: once cash reached a household, even honest farmers would spend it unwisely;

sentences.zh: 及其納錢，雖富民不免違限。

translations.literal: when it came time to repay, even wealthy households could not avoid missing deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: and when repayment came due, even prosperous families would miss their deadlines.

sentences.zh: 如此則鞭笞必用，州縣多事矣。

translations.literal: If so, the lash would necessarily be employed and prefectures and counties would have many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: The result would be floggings across the countryside and endless trouble for local officials.

sentences.zh: 唐劉晏掌國計，未嘗有所假貸。

translations.literal: Tang's Liu Yan managed the national accounts and never made any loans.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times Liu Yan had run national finance without ever making state loans.

sentences.zh: 有尤之者，晏曰：『使民僥幸得錢，非國之福；

translations.literal: Some blamed him for this; Yan said: "Letting the people by lucky chance obtain money is not the state's blessing;
translations.idiomatic: When criticized, Liu Yan said, "Handing cash to people on easy terms is no blessing for the state;

sentences.zh: 使吏倚法督責，非民之便。

translations.literal: making clerks rely on law to supervise and compel payment is not the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: and having clerks enforce repayment by law is no convenience for the people."

sentences.zh: 吾雖未嘗假貸，而四方豐凶貴賤，知之未嘗逾時。

translations.literal: Though I have never made loans, throughout the four directions abundance, famine, dearth, and cheapness—I knew them never beyond timely notice.
translations.idiomatic: I never lent, yet I always knew within the hour whether grain was plentiful or scarce, cheap or dear in every quarter of the empire."

sentences.zh: 有賤必糴，有貴必糶，以此四方無甚貴甚賤之病，安用貸為？

translations.literal: When cheap, always buying; when dear, always selling—by this the four directions had no affliction of extreme dearth or extreme cheapness; why need loans?
translations.idiomatic: When prices fell I bought; when they rose I sold—and so the realm never suffered extreme scarcity or glut. What need was there for loans?"

sentences.zh: 』晏之言，漢常平法耳，公誠能行之，晏之功可立俟也。

translations.literal: Yan's words were simply the Han Ever-Normal law; if you, sir, can truly implement it, Yan's achievement can be awaited at once.
translations.idiomatic: That is simply the Han Ever-Normal system. Implement that, and you will match Liu Yan without lending a copper coin."

sentences.zh: 」安石自此逾月不言青苗。

translations.literal: From this Anshi for more than a month did not speak of Green Sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said nothing more about Green Sprouts for over a month.

sentences.zh: 會河北轉運司幹當公事王廣廉召議事，廣廉嘗奏乞度僧牒數千道為本錢，於陝西轉運司私行青苗法，春散秋斂，與安石意合。

translations.literal: It happened that Hebei Transport Commission handler Wang Guanglian was summoned to discuss affairs; Guanglian had once memorialized requesting several thousand monk certificates as capital and privately implemented the Green Sprouts law at the Shaanxi Transport Commission—spring disbursement, autumn collection—in accord with Anshi's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Guanglian of the Hebei transport commission was called in for consultation. He had once sought permission to raise capital by selling thousands of ordination certificates and had quietly run a Green Sprouts program in Shaanxi—loans in spring, collection in autumn—matching Wang Anshi's design.

sentences.zh: 至是，請施行之河北，於是安石決意行之，而常平、廣惠倉之法遂變而為青苗矣。

translations.literal: At this time he requested implementation in Hebei; thereupon Anshi resolved to carry it out, and the Ever-Normal and Broad Relief granary methods thereby changed into Green Sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: He now asked to extend the scheme to Hebei. Wang Anshi committed fully to it, and the Ever-Normal and Broad Relief granaries became the Green Sprouts program.

sentences.zh: 蘇轍以議不合罷。

translations.literal: Su Zhe was dismissed because his views did not accord.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe was removed for dissent.

sentences.zh: 而諸路提舉官往往迎合安石之意，務以多散為功。

translations.literal: Yet the overseeing officials of all circuits often catered to Anshi's intent, striving to take wide disbursement as achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit overseers competed to please Wang by disbursing as much money as possible.

sentences.zh: 富民不願取，貧者乃欲得之，即令隨戶等高下品配，又令貧富相兼，十人為保首。

translations.literal: Wealthy households did not wish to receive loans; the poor then wished to obtain them—they were ordered to allot by household rank high and low, and also ordered rich and poor to be combined, ten persons with one guarantee head.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families refused the loans while poor ones wanted them, so officials graded allotments by household rank and grouped ten households—rich and poor mixed—with one guarantor.

sentences.zh: 王廣廉在河北，一等戶給十五千，等而下之，至五等猶給一千，民間喧然不以為便。

translations.literal: Wang Guanglian in Hebei gave first-rank households fifteen thousand, descending by rank until fifth-rank still received one thousand; among the people there was uproar and they did not consider it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei Wang Guanglian gave fifteen thousand cash to first-rank households, tapering down to one thousand even for fifth-rank families—and the public outcry made clear the scheme was no benefit.

sentences.zh: 廣廉入奏謂民皆歡呼感德，然言不便者甚眾。

translations.literal: Guanglian entered and memorialized saying the people all shouted in joy and felt gratitude, yet those who said it was inconvenient were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Guanglian reported to court that the people cheered in gratitude, though complaints were widespread.

sentences.zh: 右正言李常、孫覺乞詔有司毋以強民。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrator Li Chang and Sun Jue requested an edict ordering the responsible offices not to coerce the people.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators Li Chang and Sun Jue asked the throne to forbid officials from forcing loans on unwilling borrowers.

sentences.zh: 時提舉府界常平事侯叔獻屢督提點府界縣鎮呂景散錢，景以畿縣各有屯兵，歲入課利僅能贍給；

translations.literal: At the time Overseer of Metropolitan District Ever-Normal affairs Hou Shuxian repeatedly pressed Metropolitan District Intendant Lü Jing to disburse money; Jing said the capital counties each had garrison troops and yearly tax revenues barely sufficed to supply them;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shuxian, overseer of Ever-Normal stores in the capital district, kept pressing Intendant Lü Jing to lend out cash. Jing replied that garrison costs already consumed the counties' entire tax yield;

sentences.zh: 又民戶嘗貸糧五十餘萬石，尚悉以聞；

translations.literal: moreover, civilian households had once borrowed more than five hundred thousand shi of grain, which he had still fully reported;
translations.idiomatic: that more than five hundred thousand shi of grain was already on loan to farmers, which he had duly reported;

sentences.zh: 今條例司又以買陝西鹽鈔錢五十萬緡為青苗錢給散，恐民力不堪。

translations.literal: now the Regulations Bureau also wanted to use five hundred thousand strings from Shaanxi salt-certificate purchases as Green Sprouts money for disbursement—he feared the people's strength could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: and that the bureau now wanted to add five hundred thousand strings from Shaanxi salt-certificate purchases as Green Sprouts funds—more than the people could possibly repay.

sentences.zh: 詔送條例司，召提舉司官至中書戒諭之。

translations.literal: An edict sent the matter to the Regulations Bureau and summoned the overseers to the Secretariat for admonition.
translations.idiomatic: The throne referred the matter to the bureau and summoned the overseers to the Secretariat for a reprimand.

sentences.zh: 王安石言：「若此，諸路必顧望，不敢推行新法，第令條例司指揮。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi said: "If so, all circuits will surely hesitate and look back, not daring to implement the new laws; merely order the Regulations Bureau to direct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi objected: "That will make every circuit hang back from implementing reform. Leave direction to the Regulations Bureau alone.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The throne assented."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed."

sentences.zh: 三年，判大名府韓琦言：

translations.literal: In the third year, Grand Councilor of Daming Prefecture Han Qi said:
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining, Han Qi, prefect of Daming, memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣準散青苗詔書，務在惠小民，不使兼並乘急以要倍息，而公家無所利其入。

translations.literal: Your subject, following the edict on dispersing Green Sprouts, aims to benefit small commoners, not to let consolidators seize urgency to demand doubled interest, while the public house profits nothing from its intake.
translations.idiomatic: The edict on Green Sprouts promised relief for small farmers, protection against usurious landlords, and no profit for the state.

sentences.zh: 今所立條約，乃自鄉戶一等而下皆立借錢貫陌，三等以上更許增借，坊郭戶有物業勝質當者亦依鄉戶例支借。

translations.literal: Now the regulations established require loan quotas in strings from first-rank rural households downward; third rank and above may borrow more; urban households with property exceeding pledges likewise receive loans by rural precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The new rules fixed loan quotas for every rural household down to the lowest rank, allowed upper ranks to borrow more, and extended the same terms to wealthy townspeople.

sentences.zh: 且鄉村上等戶並坊郭有物業者，乃從來兼並之家，今令多借之錢，一千令納一千三百，則是官自放錢取息，與初詔絕相違戾。

translations.literal: Moreover, upper rural households and urban households with property were always the consolidating households; now ordering them larger loans—one thousand requiring repayment of one thousand three hundred—is the government itself lending money and taking interest, utterly at odds with the original edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those upper rural and urban households were precisely the moneylenders the policy was meant to restrain. Forcing them to borrow at thirty percent interest made the state itself a usurer—in direct violation of the original decree.

sentences.zh: 又條約雖禁抑勒，然須得上戶為甲頭以任之，民愚不慮久遠，請時甚易，納時甚難。

translations.literal: Moreover, though the regulations forbade coercion, yet upper households had to serve as guarantee heads and bear responsibility; the people, foolish, did not consider the long term—applying was very easy, repaying very hard.
translations.idiomatic: The rules banned coercion in name, but required well-off guarantors for every loan group. Farmers thought only of the easy cash at borrowing time, not the hard repayment ahead.

sentences.zh: 故自製下以來，上下惶惑，皆謂若不抑散，則上戶必不願請；

translations.literal: Therefore from the time the system was enacted, above and below were alarmed and perplexed—all saying that unless forced to disburse, upper households surely would not wish to apply;
translations.idiomatic: Since the program began, officials and commoners alike had feared that without compulsion prosperous households would never borrow,

sentences.zh: 近下等第與無業客戶雖或願請，必難催納。

translations.literal: lower ranks and propertyless clients, though sometimes wishing to apply, would surely be hard to press for repayment.
translations.idiomatic: while poorer applicants who did want the money would surely default.

sentences.zh: 將來必有行刑督索，及勒幹係書手、典押、耆戶長同保均陪之患。

translations.literal: In the future there would necessarily be the affliction of imposing punishment to supervise collection, and compelling involved clerks, jailers, elders, and village heads within the same guarantee to share equal liability.
translations.idiomatic: Sooner or later there would be torture to collect debts, with clerks, jailers, elders, and guarantors all held jointly liable.

sentences.zh: 去歲河朔豐稔，米斗不過七八十錢，若乘時多斂，俟貴而糶，不唯合古制，無失陷，兼民被實惠，亦足收其羨贏。

translations.literal: Last year the Yellow River north was abundantly harvested; a dou of rice was no more than seventy or eighty cash. If one gathered more at the opportune time and waited until dear to sell—not only accorded with ancient institutions without loss, but the people received real benefit and surplus profit could also be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the north had a bumper harvest—rice at seventy or eighty cash a dou. Buying grain then and selling when prices rose would have honored the ancient Ever-Normal system, protected the harvest, helped the people, and still yielded a surplus for the state.

sentences.zh: 今諸倉方糴而提舉司已亟止之，意在移此糴本盡為青苗錢，則三分之息可為己功，豈暇更恤斯民久遠之患？

translations.literal: Now the granaries had just begun buying when the overseers urgently stopped it—the intent being to shift all this purchase capital entirely into Green Sprouts money so that three-fen interest could count as their achievement; how could they spare concern for this people's long-term afflictions?
translations.idiomatic: Instead overseers halted grain purchases precisely to redirect those funds into Green Sprouts loans—thirty percent interest counted as their achievement, with no thought for the harm ahead?

sentences.zh: 若謂陝西嘗行其法，官有所得而民以為便，此乃轉運司因軍儲有闕，適自冬及春雨雪及時，麥苗滋盛，定見成熟，行於一時可也。

translations.literal: If one says Shaanxi once implemented the law, the government gained and the people found it convenient—this was the transport commission because military stores were deficient; it happened from winter through spring that rain and snow came timely, wheat sprouts flourished lushly, and ripening was assured—it could be done for one season.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi pilot succeeded only because military grain stores ran short and timely rains promised a good wheat crop—it was a one-season emergency measure, not a permanent model.

sentences.zh: 今乃建官置司，以為每歲常行之法，而取利三分，豈陝西權宜之比哉？

translations.literal: Now erecting offices and establishing bureaus, treating it as a law to be carried out every year, and taking three-fen interest—how is this comparable to Shaanxi's expedient measure?
translations.idiomatic: To build a permanent bureaucracy around thirty-percent interest was nothing like Shaanxi's temporary expedient?

sentences.zh: 兼初詔且於京東、淮南、河北三路試行，俟有緒方推之他路。

translations.literal: Moreover, the initial edict was only to trial it in Hebei East, Huainan, and Hebei three circuits, waiting until there was order before extending to other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The original edict had limited the trial to Hebei, Hebei East, and Huainan, to expand only after results were in.

sentences.zh: 今三路未集，而遽盡於諸路置使，非陛下憂民、祖宗惠下之意。

translations.literal: Now the three circuits were not yet consolidated, yet hastily overseers were placed in all circuits—this was not Your Majesty's intent to care for the people or the ancestral emperors' intent to show grace to those below.
translations.idiomatic: To appoint overseers empire-wide before the pilot circuits had even reported violates both Your Majesty's care for the people and the spirit of our ancestors' benevolence.

sentences.zh: 乞盡罷提舉官，第委提點刑獄官依常平舊法施行。

translations.literal: Your subject begs to abolish all overseeing officials entirely and merely commission judicial intendant officials to implement according to the Ever-Normal old law.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to abolish the overseers and restore the old Ever-Normal system under the judicial intendants.

sentences.zh: 帝袖出琦奏示執政曰：「琦真忠臣，朕始謂可以利民，不意乃害民如此。

translations.literal: The emperor took Qi's memorial from his sleeve and showed the chief ministers, saying: "Qi is a true loyal minister. I at first thought it could benefit the people; I did not expect it would harm the people so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor produced Han Qi's memorial for the chief ministers. "Han Qi is a true loyal minister. I thought this policy would help the people. I had no idea it would hurt them like this.

sentences.zh: 且坊郭安得青苗，而使者亦強與之？

translations.literal: Moreover, how should urban wards receive Green Sprouts, yet the envoys also forcibly give it to them?
translations.idiomatic: Urban wards aren't even supposed to get crop loans—why are envoys forcing money on them?"

sentences.zh: 」安石勃然進曰：「苟從其所欲，雖坊郭何害？

translations.literal: Anshi flushed and stepped forward, saying: "If one follows what they desire, even urban wards—what harm?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi flushed and stepped forward. "If they want the money, what harm is there in lending to townspeople?"

sentences.zh: 」因難琦奏，曰：「陛下修常平法以助民，至於收息，亦周公遺法也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he challenged Qi's memorial, saying: "Your Majesty is restoring the Ever-Normal law to aid the people; as for collecting interest, that too is the Duke of Zhou's transmitted law.
translations.idiomatic: He refuted Han Qi's arguments. "Your Majesty restores Ever-Normal stores to help the people. Collecting interest is itself a practice handed down from the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 如桑弘羊籠天下貨財以奉人主私用，乃可謂興利之臣；

translations.literal: Like Sang Hongyang monopolizing all under heaven's goods and wealth to supply the ruler's private use—that alone may be called a minister who raises profit;
translations.idiomatic: Sang Hongyang, who monopolized the empire's wealth for the emperor's private purse—that was a 'profit-seeking minister.'

sentences.zh: 今抑兼並，振貧弱，置官理財，非所以佐私欲，安可謂興利之臣乎？

translations.literal: now restraining consolidation, invigorating poor and weak, establishing officials to manage finances—not to aid private desire—how can this be called a minister who raises profit?
translations.idiomatic: Restraining landlords, strengthening the poor, and appointing officials to manage public finance—this serves no private greed. How can you call that profit-seeking?"

sentences.zh: 」曾公亮、陳升之皆言坊郭不當俵錢，與安石論難久之而罷。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang and Chen Shengzhi both said urban wards should not receive allocated money; they debated Anshi at length and then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang and Chen Shengzhi both argued that townspeople should not receive allocated loans; they wrangled with Wang Anshi at length before the meeting broke up.

sentences.zh: 帝終以琦說為疑，安石遂稱疾不出。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately took Qi's account as grounds for doubt; Anshi then claimed illness and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remained troubled by Han Qi's account, and Wang Anshi pleaded illness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 帝諭執政罷青苗法，公亮、升之欲即奉詔，趙抃獨欲俟安石出自罷之，連日不決。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the chief ministers to abolish the Green Sprouts law; Gongliang and Shengzhi wished immediately to obey the edict; Zhao Bian alone wished to wait until Anshi emerged and then abolish it—for many days no decision.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers to cancel Green Sprouts. Zeng and Chen wanted to obey at once, but Zhao Bian insisted on waiting for Wang Anshi to return—and for days the court could decide nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝更以為疑，因令呂惠卿諭旨起安石，安石入謝。

translations.literal: The emperor grew more doubtful; therefore he had Lü Huiqing convey the edict to summon Anshi; Anshi entered and gave thanks.
translations.idiomatic: More uncertain than ever, the emperor sent Lü Huiqing to fetch Wang back. Wang appeared at court to thank the throne.

sentences.zh: 既視事，志氣愈悍，麵責公亮等，由是持新法益堅。

translations.literal: Once he resumed duties, his spirit grew fiercer; he faced and rebuked Gongliang and others; from this he held to the new laws more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Once back at work his temper was fiercer than before. He berated Zeng Gongliang to his face and dug in harder on every reform.

sentences.zh: 詔以琦奏付製置條例司，條例司疏列琦奏而辨析其不然。

translations.literal: An edict handed Qi's memorial to the Fiscal Reform Bureau; the bureau laid out Qi's memorial item by item and analyzed why it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: The throne referred Han Qi's memorial to the Fiscal Reform Bureau, which issued a point-by-point rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 琦復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Qi again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 「製置司多刪去臣元奏要語，唯舉大概，用偏辭曲難，及引《周禮》「國服為息」之說，文其謬妄，上以欺罔聖聽，下以愚弄天下。

translations.literal: "The Fiscal Bureau deleted many key phrases from my original memorial, citing only the general outline, using partial language and tortuous refutation, and citing the Zhou Rites doctrine of "national service as interest" to ornament its errors and deceptions—above to deceive Your Sacred Hearing, below to fool all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: "The bureau stripped my memorial of its essential arguments and answered with selective quotations. It cites the Zhou Rites on "national service as interest" to dress up absurdity—deceiving Your Majesty above and misleading the empire below.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為周公立太平之法，必無剝民取利之理，但漢儒解釋或有異同。

translations.literal: Your subject privately considers that the Duke of Zhou established laws of great peace—there surely cannot be a principle of stripping the people to take profit; only Han scholars' explanations may differ.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou's order was for great peace, not for stripping the people of profit—though Han commentators may disagree on details.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》「園廛二十而稅一，唯漆林之征二十而五」，鄭康成乃約此法，謂：「從官貸錢若受園廛之地，貸萬錢者出息五百。

translations.literal: The Zhou Rites states: "Garden lots taxed one in twenty, only lacquer groves taxed five in twenty"; Zheng Xuan accordingly condensed this method, saying: "Borrowing money from the office as if receiving garden-lot land—one who borrows ten thousand cash pays five hundred interest.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Rites taxes garden plots at five percent and lacquer groves at twenty-five percent. Zheng Xuan inferred from this that official loans carried five percent interest on ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 」賈公彥廣其說，謂：「如此則近郊十一者，萬錢期出息一千，遠郊二十而三者，萬錢期出息一千五百，甸、稍、縣、都之民，萬錢期出息二千。

translations.literal: Jia Gongyan expanded his doctrine, saying: "If so, then for the near suburbs taxed eleven in a hundred, ten thousand cash expected one thousand interest; for distant suburbs taxed three in twenty, ten thousand expected one thousand five hundred; for the inner, outer, county, and capital domains' people, ten thousand expected two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Gongyan extended the logic: near suburbs would pay ten percent, distant suburbs fifteen percent, and the outer domains twenty percent on a loan of ten thousand."

sentences.zh: 」如此，則須漆林之戶取貸，方出息二千五百，當時未必如此。

translations.literal: Even so, only lacquer-grove households taking loans would pay two thousand five hundred interest—the age may not have been thus.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the highest rate that would mean twenty-five percent—and only for lacquer growers. The Zhou economy almost certainly did not work that way.

sentences.zh: 今放青苗錢，凡春貸十千，半年之內便令納利二千，秋再放十千，至歲終又令納利二千，則是貸萬錢者，不問遠近，歲令出息四千。

translations.literal: Now disbursing Green Sprouts money: in spring ten thousand is lent; within half a year two thousand interest is demanded; in autumn ten thousand is lent again; by year's end another two thousand interest is demanded—thus for one who borrows ten thousand cash, regardless of near or far, the year demands four thousand interest.
translations.idiomatic: Green Sprouts lends ten thousand in spring and demands two thousand interest within six months, then lends ten thousand again in autumn and demands another two thousand by year's end—forty percent on ten thousand, everywhere alike.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》至遠之地止出息二千，今青苗取息過《周禮》一倍，製置司言比《同禮》取息已不為多，是欺罔聖聽，且謂天下之人不能辨也。

translations.literal: The Zhou Rites at the farthest places stops at two thousand interest; now Green Sprouts takes interest exceeding the Zhou Rites by double. The Fiscal Bureau says that compared with the Tong Rites, taking interest is already not much—this is deceiving Sacred Hearing and moreover treating all under heaven as unable to discern.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Rites cap interest at twenty percent even in the farthest domains. Green Sprouts doubles that—yet the bureau insists its rates are modest by Zhou standards, as if the entire empire were too stupid to tell the difference.

sentences.zh: 且古今異宜，《周禮》所載有不可施於今者，其事非一。

translations.literal: Moreover, ancient and modern differ in what is fitting; what the Zhou Rites records has much that cannot be applied today—not one matter alone.
translations.idiomatic: Times change. Much of the Zhou Rites cannot be applied today—and this is only one example.

sentences.zh: 若謂泉府一職今可施行，則製置司何獨舉注疏貸錢取息一事，以詆天下之公言哉？

translations.literal: If one says the Treasury Office post can be implemented today, then why does the Fiscal Bureau alone cite the commentary on lending money and taking interest, to slander public discourse throughout the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If the Treasury Office is truly revivable today, why does the bureau cherry-pick only the passage on loan interest to silence every critic in the empire?

sentences.zh: 康成又注云：「王莽時貸以治產業者，但計所贏受息，無過歲什一。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan further annotated: "In Wang Mang's time, loans for managing industries—only the profit gained was charged interest, not exceeding one-tenth per year.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also notes that under Wang Mang, loans for productive enterprise charged interest only on actual profits, capped at ten percent per year."

sentences.zh: 」公彥疏云：「莽時雖計本多少為定，及其催科，唯所贏多少。

translations.literal: Jia Gongyan in commentary said: "In Mang's time, though the principal more or less was fixed as standard, when pressing collection, only the profit more or less counted.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Gongyan explains that Wang Mang fixed the principal in advance but collected only on what the borrower actually earned."

sentences.zh: 假令萬錢歲贏萬錢催一千，贏五千催五百，餘皆據利催什一。

translations.literal: Suppose ten thousand cash yearly profit ten thousand cash—press one thousand; profit five thousand—press five hundred; the rest all according to profit press one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand profit meant one thousand interest; five thousand profit meant five hundred—always one-tenth of gains."

sentences.zh: 」若贏錢更少，則納息更薄，比今青苗取利尤為寬少。

translations.literal: If profit was even less, then interest paid was thinner—compared with today's Green Sprouts taking profit it was still more lenient and lesser.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller profits meant smaller payments—far gentler than Green Sprouts.

sentences.zh: 而王莽之外，上自兩漢，下及有唐，更不聞有貸錢取利之法。

translations.literal: Outside Wang Mang, from the two Han dynasties above down through Tang, one no longer hears of a law of lending money and taking interest.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Wang Mang, no dynasty from Han through Tang ever codified state lending at interest.

sentences.zh: 今制置司遇堯、舜之主，不以二帝、三王之道上裨聖政，而貸錢取利更過莽時，此天下不得不指以為非，而老臣不可以不辨也。

translations.literal: Now the Fiscal Bureau, encountering rulers like Yao and Shun, does not use the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings to augment sagely governance above, but instead lends money for interest exceeding Mang's time—this all under heaven cannot but point to as wrong, and your aged minister cannot but clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Faced with a ruler as wise as Yao and Shun, the bureau offers nothing from the sages' governance but a lending scheme worse than Wang Mang's—an outrage your aging servant must answer.

sentences.zh: 況今天下田稅已重，固非《周禮》什一之法，更有農具、牛皮、鹽曲、鞋錢之類，凡十餘目，謂之雜錢。

translations.literal: Moreover, today land tax under heaven is already heavy—it is certainly not the Zhou Rites' one-tenth law; moreover there are farm implements, ox hide, salt yeast, shoe money and the like, more than ten categories in all, called miscellaneous levies.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax already exceeds the Zhou ideal of one tenth, with more than a dozen miscellaneous levies—farm tools, ox hides, salt yeast, shoe fees, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 每夏秋起納，官中更以綢絹斛斗低估，令民以此雜錢折納。

translations.literal: Each summer and autumn when collection began, the government further undervalued silk and grain measures, ordering the people to use these miscellaneous levies to pay in conversion.
translations.idiomatic: Each summer and autumn the government undercounts silk and grain, forcing farmers to make up the gap in miscellaneous cash payments.

sentences.zh: 又歲散官鹽與民，謂之蠶鹽，折納絹帛。

translations.literal: Also each year government salt was dispersed to the people, called silkworm salt, converted to payment in silk bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the state distributes salt—the so-called silkworm salt—payable in silk cloth.

sentences.zh: 更有預買、和買綢絹，如此之類，不可悉舉，皆《周禮》田稅什一之外加斂之物，取利已厚，傷農已深，奈何又引《周禮》「國服為息」之說，謂放青苗錢取利乃周公太平已試之法？

translations.literal: Moreover there are advance purchase and harmonized purchase of silk—such categories cannot all be listed; all are levies added beyond the Zhou Rites' land tax of one-tenth; profit taken is already thick, harm to farmers already deep—how then again cite the Zhou Rites "national service as interest" doctrine, saying that disbursing Green Sprouts money for interest is the Duke of Zhou's great peace already tested method?
translations.idiomatic: Advance purchase and harmonized purchase of silk add yet more—I cannot name them all. These burdens already far exceed the Zhou tithe and already crush the farmer. How dare the bureau invoke Zhou Rites to claim Green Sprouts interest is the Duke of Zhou's own proven method?

sentences.zh: 此則誣汙聖典，蔽惑睿明，老臣得不太息而慟哭也！

translations.literal: This is slandering and defiling the sacred canon, obscuring and confusing sagacious clarity—can your aged minister not sigh deeply and mourn in anguish!
translations.idiomatic: This defiles the classics and obscures your sagacity—I can only sigh and weep in grief!

sentences.zh: 製置司又謂常平舊法亦糶與坊郭之人。

translations.literal: The Fiscal Bureau also says the Ever-Normal old law likewise sold to urban people.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau claims the old Ever-Normal system also sold grain to townspeople.

sentences.zh: 坊郭有物力戶未嘗零糴常平倉斛斗，此蓋欲多借錢與坊郭有業之人，以望收利之多，妄稱《周禮》以為無都邑鄙野之限，以文其曲說，唯陛下詳之。」
