translations.literal: Urban households with property strength never bought odd measures from Ever-Normal granaries—this is surely wanting to lend more money to urban people with occupations, hoping to collect more profit, falsely claiming the Zhou Rites as having no limit between capital and countryside, to ornament their twisted doctrine. May Your Majesty examine this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Property-owning townspeople never bought grain by the bowl from Ever-Normal stores—the bureau only wants to lend them more cash for more interest and invents a Zhou Rites excuse to erase the difference between town and country. I beg Your Majesty to judge for yourself."

sentences.zh: 樞密使文彥博亦數言不便，帝曰：「吾遣二中使親問民間，皆云甚便。

translations.literal: Palace Deputy Wen Yanbo also repeatedly spoke of inconvenience; the emperor said: "I dispatched two palace emissaries to personally inquire among the people—they all said it was very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs Commissioner Wen Yanbo also protested repeatedly. The emperor said, "I sent two palace envoys to ask the people themselves. They report universal satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 」彥博曰：「韓琦三朝宰相，不信，而信二宦者乎？

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Han Qi, grand councilor of three reigns—you do not believe him, yet you believe two eunuch attendants?
translations.idiomatic: Wen replied, "Han Qi served three reigns as grand councilor—and you trust two eunuchs instead?"

sentences.zh: 」先是，王安石陰結入內副都知張若水、押班藍元震，帝因使二人潛察府界俵錢事，還言民皆情願，無抑配者，故帝益信之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Anshi had secretly allied with Inner Deputy Director Zhang Ruoshui and Duty Shift Leader Lan Yuanzhen; the emperor therefore had the two secretly inspect metropolitan district loan allocation; they returned saying the people all willingly consented, none coerced—all the more the emperor trusted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi had privately cultivated Inner Deputy Director Zhang Ruoshui and Duty Shift Leader Lan Yuanzhen. The emperor sent them to inspect capital-district lending. They returned reporting willing borrowers and no coercion—and the emperor's faith in the program only grew.

sentences.zh: 初，群臣進讀邇英畢，帝問：「朝廷每更一事，舉朝洶洶，何也？

translations.literal: At first, after the ministers finished reading at the Zhiying Hall, the emperor asked: "Whenever the court changes one matter, the whole court is in uproar—why?
translations.idiomatic: After a lecture session at the Zhiying Hall, the emperor asked, "Why is the entire court in uproar every time we change a policy?

sentences.zh: 」司馬光曰：「青苗出息，平民為之，尚能以蠶食下戶至饑寒流離，況縣官法度之威乎？

translations.literal: Sima Guang said: "Green Sprouts interest—when commoners do it, still they can gnaw like silkworms on lower households until hunger, cold, and wandering in exile; how much more the awesome authority of county officials and state law?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang said, "Private lenders already gnaw away at poor households until families starve and scatter. What will happen when county officials enforce the law?"

sentences.zh: 」呂惠卿曰：「青苗法願則取之，不願不強也。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing said: "The Green Sprouts law—if they wish, take it; if they do not wish, do not force.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing said, "Green Sprouts is voluntary—no one is forced to borrow."

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「愚民知取債之利，不知還債之害，非獨縣官不強，富民亦不強也。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Foolish commoners know the benefit of taking debt, not the harm of repaying debt—even county officials do not force them, nor do wealthy households force them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang said, "People see the benefit of borrowing but not the pain of repayment. Rich lenders do not have to force anyone either—the poor beg for the money."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「陝西行之久，民不以為病。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shaanxi has carried it out long; the people do not regard it as affliction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shaanxi has run it for years without complaint."

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「臣陝西人也，見其病不見其利。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Your subject is a Shaanxi man—I see its affliction, not its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang said, "I am from Shaanxi. I saw the harm, not the benefit."

sentences.zh: 朝廷初不許，有司尚能以病民，況法許之乎！

translations.literal: The court at first did not permit it, yet responsible officials could still afflict the people—how much more when the law permits it!
translations.idiomatic: Officials abused the people even when the law forbade it—what will they do once it is legal!

sentences.zh: 」及拜官樞密副使，光上章力辭至六七，曰：「帝誠能罷製置條例司，追還提舉官，不行青苗、助役等法，雖不用臣，臣受賜多矣。

translations.literal: When appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, Guang submitted memorials forcefully declining six or seven times, saying: "If Your Majesty can truly abolish the Fiscal Reform Bureau, recall the overseeing officials, and not implement Green Sprouts, corvée substitution, and the like—though you do not employ your subject, your subject has received great grace.
translations.idiomatic: When offered the vice commissionership of military affairs, Sima Guang refused six or seven times, writing: "If Your Majesty abolishes the Fiscal Reform Bureau, recalls the overseers, and cancels Green Sprouts and corvée substitution, I need no office—I will still owe you a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 不然，終不敢受命。

translations.literal: If not so, in the end your subject dares not accept the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I dare not accept the appointment."

sentences.zh: 」竟出知永興軍。

translations.literal: In the end he was sent out as prefect of Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was posted as prefect of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 當是時，爭青苗錢者甚眾，翰林學士範鎮言：「陛下初詔雲公家無所利其入，今提舉司以戶等給錢，皆令出三分之息，物議紛紜，皆云自古未有天子開課場者。

translations.literal: At this time those disputing Green Sprouts money were very numerous; Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen said: "Your Majesty's initial edict stated the public house profited nothing from intake; now overseers allocate money by household rank and all are made to pay three-fen interest; public discussion is tangled—all say since antiquity there never was an emperor who opened a interest shop.
translations.idiomatic: Opposition was widespread. Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen said, "Your first edict promised the state would take no profit. Now overseers lend by household rank at thirty percent interest. Public chatter says no emperor since antiquity ever ran a pawnshop for the throne.

sentences.zh: 民雖至愚，不可不畏。

translations.literal: The people, though utterly foolish, cannot but be feared.
translations.idiomatic: However simple the people may seem, they are not to be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 」後以言不行致仕。

translations.literal: Later, because his words were not followed, he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: When his advice went unheeded he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 台諫官呂公著、孫覺、李常、張戩、程顥等皆以論青苗罷黜。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and censorial officials Lü Gongzhu, Sun Jue, Li Chang, Zhang Zhan, Cheng Hao, and others were all dismissed for discussing Green Sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials Lü Gongzhu, Sun Jue, Li Chang, Zhang Zhan, Cheng Hao, and others were all removed for opposing Green Sprouts.

sentences.zh: 知亳州富弼、知青州歐陽修繼韓琦論青苗之害，且持之不行，亦坐移鎮。

translations.literal: Prefect of Bozhou Fu Bi and Prefect of Qingzhou Ouyang Xiu, following Han Qi in discussing Green Sprouts' harm and moreover refusing to implement it, also suffered transfer to other posts.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi of Bozhou and Ouyang Xiu of Qingzhou followed Han Qi in denouncing Green Sprouts and refusing to enforce it—they too were transferred.

sentences.zh: 知陳留縣薑潛之官才數月，青苗令下，潛即榜於縣門，又移之鄉村，各三日無人至，遂撤榜付吏曰：「民不願矣！

translations.literal: Magistrate of Chenliu County Jiang Qian had held office only a few months when the Green Sprouts order came down; Qian immediately posted notices at the county gate and moved them to villages—three days each, no one came; thereupon he removed the notices and handed them to clerks, saying: "The people do not wish it!
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qian had been magistrate of Chenliu only a few months when the Green Sprouts order arrived. He posted notices at the county gate and in every village. After three days at each site with no applicants, he took the notices down and told his clerks, "The people do not want these loans!

sentences.zh: 」府、寺疑潛壅令，使其屬按驗，無違令者。

translations.literal: The prefecture and commission suspected Qian had obstructed the order and had subordinates investigate—none violated the order.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural and judicial commissioners suspected Jiang of blocking the policy and sent investigators—but found no violation of the order.

sentences.zh: 潛知不免，即移疾去。

translations.literal: Qian knew he could not escape punishment and immediately pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing punishment was inevitable, Jiang Qian at once claimed illness and left office.

sentences.zh: 知山陰縣陳舜俞不肯奉行，移狀自劾曰：「方今小民匱乏，願貸之人往往有之。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shanyin County Chen Shunyu refused to implement it, submitted a memorial impeaching himself, saying: 「At present the common people are destitute, and those who wish to borrow are often found.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shunyu, magistrate of Shanyin County, refused to enforce the policy and submitted a self-impeachment memorial: 「The common people are now in dire want, and many would gladly take a loan.

sentences.zh: 譬如孺子見飴蜜，孰不染指爭食？

translations.literal: It is like children seeing honey and candy—who does not dip a finger and scramble to eat?
translations.idiomatic: It is like children spying sweets—who would not reach out and fight to taste them?

sentences.zh: 然父母疾止之，恐其積甘足以生病。

translations.literal: Yet parents swiftly stop them, fearing that too much sweetness will be enough to cause illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet parents quickly forbid it, lest the accumulating sweetness make them sick.

sentences.zh: 故耆老戒其鄉黨，父兄誨其子弟，未嘗不以貸貰為不善治生。

translations.literal: Therefore elders admonish their villages and neighborhoods, fathers and elder brothers instruct sons and younger brothers, never failing to treat borrowing money as poor management of livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Elders warn their neighbors, fathers and elder brothers teach their sons, always calling borrowing a sign of bad household management.

sentences.zh: 今乃官自出舉，誘以便利，督以威刑，非王道之舉也。

translations.literal: Now the government itself issues loans, enticing with convenience, compelling with fearful punishments—this is not the conduct of kingly governance.
translations.idiomatic: Now the state itself lends money, luring people with convenience and driving them with harsh penalties—this is no kingly way to govern.

sentences.zh: 況正月放夏料，五月放秋料，而所斂亦在當月，百姓得錢便出息輸納，實無所利。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the first month the summer installment is released, in the fifth month the autumn installment; yet collection also comes in that same month—the people receive money and immediately pay interest, truly gaining no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, the summer tranche is disbursed in the first month and the autumn tranche in the fifth, yet repayment is due the same month; peasants get the cash only to pay interest at once, gaining nothing in fact.

sentences.zh: 是使民一取青苗錢，終身以及世世一歲嘗兩輸息錢，乃別為一賦以弊生民也。

translations.literal: This makes the people, once they take Green Sprouts money, for life and for generation after generation in one year once pay interest twice—it becomes a separate levy to afflict the living people.
translations.idiomatic: One Green Sprouts loan binds a household for life—and generations after—for a year in which interest is paid twice; it becomes a separate tax that ruins the people.

sentences.zh: 」坐謫南康軍鹽酒稅。

translations.literal: 」For this he was demoted to the salt-and-wine tax post at Nankang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was banished to supervise the salt-and-wine tax at Nankang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 陝西轉運副使陳繹止環、慶等六州毋散青苗錢，且留常平倉物以備用，條例司劾其罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Transport Deputy Commissioner Chen Ze ordered the six prefectures of Huan, Qing, and others not to disburse Green Sprouts money and to retain Ever-Normal Granary goods for emergency use; the Legislation Commission impeached him for crime, and an edict released him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ze, deputy transport commissioner for Shaanxi, barred six prefectures including Huan and Qing from issuing Green Sprouts loans and kept Ever-Normal stores in reserve. The Legislation Commission charged him, but an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 五月，製置三司條例司罷歸中書，以常平新法付司農寺，命集賢校理呂惠卿同判寺，兼領田役水利。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Fiscal Reform Commission was abolished and returned to the Secretariat; the new Ever-Normal laws were entrusted to the Ministry of Revenues; Academician-Editor Lü Huiqing was ordered as concurrent Administrator of the Ministry, also overseeing field corvée and irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Fiscal Reform Commission was dissolved and restored to the Secretariat. Ever-Normal reforms passed to the Ministry of Revenues, with Lü Huiqing as its concurrent chief, also supervising field corvée and waterworks.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝患俵常平官吏多違法，王安石請縣專置一主簿，主給納役錢及常平，不過五百員，費錢三十萬貫耳。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Emperor worried that officials distributing Ever-Normal funds often violated the law; Wang Anshi requested that each county specially appoint one registrar to manage corvée payments and Ever-Normal affairs—no more than five hundred posts, costing only three hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor grew troubled that Ever-Normal officers frequently broke the law. Wang Anshi proposed a dedicated registrar in each county for corvée and Ever-Normal duties—at most five hundred posts, for just three hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝以久旱為憂，翰林學士承旨韓維言：「畿縣近督青苗甚急，往往鞭撻取足，民至伐桑為薪以易錢。

translations.literal: The Emperor, worried by prolonged drought, Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy Han Wei said: 「Near the capital, collection of Green Sprouts has recently been pressed very urgently—often with beating to make quotas; the people even cut mulberry trees for firewood to exchange for money.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious about the long drought, Han Wei, Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, said: 「Around the capital, Green Sprouts collection has grown fierce—officials whip people to fill quotas; peasants are felling mulberries for firewood just to raise the cash.

sentences.zh: 旱災之際，重罹此苦。

translations.literal: In a time of drought disaster, they suffer this hardship again.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of drought, they must endure this torment on top of famine.

sentences.zh: 」帝頗感悟。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor was somewhat moved to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply shaken.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后亦嘗為帝言：「聞民間甚苦青田、助役錢，盍罷之！

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager also once spoke to the Emperor: 「I hear the people greatly suffer under Green Sprouts and corvée-assistance money—why not abolish them!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager also told the emperor: 「I hear the people are crushed by Green Sprouts and corvée-assistance payments—why not end them!

sentences.zh: 」會百姓流離，帝憂見顏色，益疑新法不便，欲罷之。

translations.literal: 」Just then the common people were displaced in flight; worry showed on the Emperor's face; he increasingly doubted the new laws' convenience and wished to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: As refugees streamed across the land, grief filled the emperor's face. He came to doubt the new laws and wanted them abolished.

sentences.zh: 安石不悅，屢求去，四月，出知江寧府。

translations.literal: Anshi was displeased, repeatedly sought to leave; in the fourth month he was sent out as prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi, displeased, repeatedly asked to resign. In the fourth month he was posted prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 然安石薦韓絳代相，仍以呂惠卿佐之，於安石所為遵守不變。

translations.literal: Yet Anshi recommended Han Jiang to replace him as Chancellor, still employing Lü Huiqing to assist; what Anshi had done continued unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, Wang Anshi recommended Han Jiang as chancellor and kept Lü Huiqing as his aide; Wang's policies went on unchanged.

sentences.zh: 既而詔諸路常平錢穀常留一半外，方得給散。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered that on all circuits Ever-Normal money and grain must always retain half before disbursement might be made.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required every circuit to keep half its Ever-Normal stores on hand before any disbursement.

sentences.zh: 兩經倚閣常平錢人戶，不得支借。

translations.literal: Households that twice had deferred Ever-Normal loans were not permitted to borrow again.
translations.idiomatic: Households that had twice deferred repayment were barred from new loans.

sentences.zh: 民間非時闕乏，許以物產為抵，依常平限輸納。

translations.literal: When the people lacked funds out of season, they were permitted to pledge produce as security and pay according to Ever-Normal deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: When peasants faced seasonal shortages, they could pledge crops as collateral and repay on the Ever-Normal schedule.

sentences.zh: 當輸錢而願輸穀若金帛者，官立中價示民。

translations.literal: When money was due but one wished to pay grain or silk and gold, the government set fair prices to show the people.
translations.idiomatic: Those who owed cash but preferred grain or cloth could pay at official fair rates.

sentences.zh: 物不盡其錢，足以錢；

translations.literal: If goods did not suffice for the money owed, cash made up the difference.
translations.idiomatic: If pledged goods fell short, cash covered the remainder.

sentences.zh: 錢不盡其物者，還其餘直。

translations.literal: If cash did not suffice for the goods, the remaining value was returned.
translations.idiomatic: If cash fell short of the goods' value, the surplus was refunded.

sentences.zh: 又聽民以金帛易穀，而有司少加金帛之直。

translations.literal: The people were also allowed to exchange gold and silk for grain, and the officials slightly marked up the value of gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants could also trade silk or gold for grain, though officials added a small premium on the metal and cloth.

sentences.zh: 六年，戶部言：「準詔諸路常平可酌三年斂散中數，取一年為格，歲終較其增虧。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Ministry of Revenue reported: 「Per edict, Ever-Normal on all circuits may weigh the median of three years' disbursement and collection, take one year as the standard, and at year's end compare increase and shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Ministry of Revenue reported: 「As ordered, each circuit should set Ever-Normal quotas from the three-year median of lending and collection, then at year's end report gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 今以錢銀穀帛貫、石、匹、兩定年額：散一千一百三萬七千七百七十二，斂一千三百九十六萬五千四百五十九。

translations.literal: Now fixing annual quotas in strings of cash, piculs of grain, bolts of cloth, and ounces of silver: disbursement 11,037,772; collection 13,965,459.
translations.idiomatic: Annual targets were set—in strings, piculs, bolts, and ounces: disbursements of 11,037,772; collections of 13,965,459.

sentences.zh: 比元豐三年散增二百一十四萬八千三百四十二，斂增一百三萬四千九百六十三；

translations.literal: Compared with Yuanfeng year three, disbursement increased by 2,148,342; collection increased by 1,034,963;
translations.idiomatic: Disbursements rose 2,148,342 over Yuanfeng 3; collections rose 1,034,963;

sentences.zh: 四年散增二百七十九萬九千九百六十四，斂虧一百九十八萬六千五百一十五。

translations.literal: In year four disbursement increased by 2,799,964; collection fell short by 1,986,515.
translations.idiomatic: In year four disbursements rose 2,799,964, while collections fell short by 1,986,515.

sentences.zh: 」詔三年四年散多斂少及散斂俱少之處，戶部下提舉司具析以聞。

translations.literal: 」An edict ordered that where in years three and four disbursement was high but collection low, or both were low, the Ministry should have supervising offices submit detailed reports.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits where lending outpaced collection—or both lagged—in those years were ordered to file detailed explanations with the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔開封府界先自豐稔畿縣立義倉法。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict ordered that within the metropolitan prefecture, beginning with fertile capital-district counties, the charity granary law be established.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the court first instituted charity granaries in the capital region, starting with the most fertile metropolitan counties.

sentences.zh: 明年，提點府界諸縣鎮公事蔡承禧言：「義倉之法，以二石而輸一斗，至為輕矣。

translations.literal: The next year Supervisor of Capital Counties and Market Affairs Cai Chenxi said: 「The charity granary law, one peck per two piculs contributed, is extremely light.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Cai Chenxi, overseer of the capital counties, said: 「The charity levy—one peck per two piculs—is already modest enough.

sentences.zh: 乞今年夏稅之始，悉令舉行。

translations.literal: I beg that from the start of this year's summer tax it be fully enforced.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that it take full effect with this summer's tax collection.

sentences.zh: 」詔可，仍以義倉隸提舉司。

translations.literal: 」An edict approved, and charity granaries were again placed under the supervising offices.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and placed charity granaries under the supervising offices.

sentences.zh: 京東西、淮南、河東、陝西路義倉以今年秋料為始，民輸稅不及鬥免輸，頒其法於川峽四路。

translations.literal: In the eastern and western capital circuits, Huainan, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits charity granaries began with this year's autumn tax; people whose tax payment was less than one peck were exempt; the law was promulgated to the four Sichuan gorges circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern capital, Huainan, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits, charity granaries began with the autumn tax; those owing less than a peck were exempt. The rule was extended to the four Sichuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，詔威、茂、黎三州罷行義倉法，以夷夏雜居，歲賦不多故也。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng year two an edict ordered Wei, Mao, and Li prefectures to cease the charity granary law, because Yi and Chinese lived intermixed and annual tax was not great.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 2 three frontier prefectures—Wei, Mao, and Li—were exempted, as Han and non-Han lived side by side and yields were too low.

sentences.zh: 八年，並罷諸路義倉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year charity granaries on all circuits were altogether abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year charity granaries were abolished throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，詔：「提舉官累年積蓄錢穀財物，盡樁作常平錢物，委提點刑獄交管，依舊常平倉法行之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou an edict said: 「Supervising officials' accumulated money, grain, and goods over many years shall all be registered as Ever-Normal funds, entrusted to judicial intendant commissioners for custody, and administered according to the former Ever-Normal Granary law.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1 an edict ordered that funds hoarded by supervising officers be reclassified as Ever-Normal stores, placed under judicial intendants, and run under the old Ever-Normal rules.

sentences.zh: 罷各縣專置主簿。

translations.literal: Specialized county registrars were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated county registrars were abolished.

sentences.zh: 」四月，再立常平錢穀給斂出息之法，限二月或正月以散及一半為額，民間絲麥豐熟，隨夏稅先納所輸之半，願伴納者止出息一分。

translations.literal: 」In the fourth month the Ever-Normal law of disbursement, collection, and interest was reestablished, limiting disbursement in the second or first month to half the quota; when silk and wheat were abundant, half the payment was made with the summer tax; those wishing to pay together owed only one percent interest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Ever-Normal lending with interest was revived, capped at half quota disbursed in January or February. Where wheat and silk flourished, half could be prepaid with the summer tax; voluntary borrowers owed only one percent interest.

sentences.zh: 左司諫王岩叟、監察御史上官均、右正言王覿、右司諫蘇轍、御史中丞劉摯交章論復行青苗之非。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Official Wang Yansou, Investigating Censor Shangguan Jun, Right Rectifier Wang Di, Right Remonstrance Official Su Che, and Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhi submitted successive memorials debating the error of restoring Green Sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou, Shangguan Jun, Wang Di, Su Che, and Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhi jointly memorialized against reviving Green Sprouts.

sentences.zh: 八月，司馬光奏：「先朝散青苗，本為利民，並取情願。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Sima Guang memorialized: 「The former court disbursed Green Sprouts to benefit the people and took only voluntary consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Sima Guang wrote: 「The previous dynasty meant Green Sprouts to help the people and relied on voluntary uptake.

sentences.zh: 後提舉官速要見功，務求多散，或舉縣追呼，或排門抄紥；

translations.literal: Later supervising officials hurried to show achievement, striving to disburse as much as possible—sometimes summoning an entire county, sometimes going door to door to pin people down;
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors then rushed for credit and pushed ever more loans—calling whole counties to account or going door to door;

sentences.zh: 亦有無賴子弟謾昧尊長，錢不入家；

translations.literal: There were also worthless sons and younger brothers deceiving their elders; the money never entered the household;
translations.idiomatic: Worthless sons tricked their elders and kept the cash;

sentences.zh: 亦有他人冒名詐請，莫知為誰，及至追催，皆歸本戶。

translations.literal: Others falsely borrowed under another's name—no one knew who was responsible—yet when collection came, all fell on the registered household.
translations.idiomatic: Strangers borrowed under false names, and when collectors came, the debt always landed on the registered household.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷深知其弊，故悉罷提舉官，不復立額考校，訪聞人情安便。

translations.literal: Now the court deeply knows these abuses, therefore altogether abolished supervising officials, no longer set quotas for examination; I hear the people's feelings are at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The court now knows these abuses well, which is why it abolished supervisors and quota audits—and I hear the people breathe easier.

sentences.zh: 欲下諸路提點刑獄，申嚴州縣抑配之禁。

translations.literal: I wish to dispatch to all circuits' judicial intendant commissioners and strictly warn prefectures and counties against forced allocation.
translations.idiomatic: I propose ordering judicial intendants on every circuit to enforce the ban on forced allocation.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: 」An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人蘇軾不書錄黃，奏曰：「熙寧之法，未嘗不禁抑配，而其害至此。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Su Shi refused to draft the recorded edict and memorialized: 「The Xining laws never failed to forbid forced allocation, yet the harm reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi, a Secretariat drafter, refused to endorse the edict and wrote: 「Even Xining's laws banned forced allocation—and still the damage was this great.

sentences.zh: 民家量入為出，雖貧亦足，若令分外得錢，則費用自廣。

translations.literal: Households measure income against outgo—even if poor they suffice; if allowed extra money, expenses naturally broaden.
translations.idiomatic: Families live within their means; even the poor get by. Give them extra cash and spending swells of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 況子弟欺謾父兄，人戶冒名詐請，似此本非抑配。

translations.literal: Moreover, when sons and younger brothers deceive fathers and elder brothers, households borrow under false names—these cases seem not forced allocation at all.
translations.idiomatic: When sons deceive fathers or loans are taken under false names, that hardly looks like forced allocation—but it is the same harm.

sentences.zh: 臣謂以散及一半為額，與熙寧無異。

translations.literal: Your servant says setting disbursement at half the quota differs in nothing from Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Capping disbursement at half the quota differs not at all from Xining policy.

sentences.zh: 今許人願請，未免設法罔民，使快一時非理之用，而不慮後日催納之患。

translations.literal: Now permitting voluntary requests still cannot avoid framing laws to mislead the people—satisfying unreasonable present wants without considering later collection's troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Calling it voluntary still means trapping people—indulgence today without heed for collection tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 二者皆非良法，相去無幾。

translations.literal: Neither is a good law; the distance between them is not great.
translations.idiomatic: Neither approach is sound; they differ little.

sentences.zh: 今已行常平糶糴之法，惠民之外，官亦稍利，何用二分之息，以賈無窮之怨？

translations.literal: Now the Ever-Normal method of selling and buying grain is already in effect—besides benefiting the people, the government also gains somewhat; why use two percent interest to buy endless resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Ever-Normal grain sales already help the people and bring the state modest profit—why court endless hatred for two percent interest?

sentences.zh: 」於是王岩叟、蘇轍、朱光庭、王覿等復言：「臣等屢有封事，乞罷青苗，皆不蒙付外。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon Wang Yansou, Su Che, Zhu Guangting, Wang Di, and others spoke again: 「We have repeatedly submitted sealed memorials begging abolition of Green Sprouts, yet none was sent out for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou, Su Che, Zhu Guangting, Wang Di, and others protested again: 「We have repeatedly asked to abolish Green Sprouts, yet the court never forwarded our memorials.

sentences.zh: 願盡付三省，公議得失。

translations.literal: We wish all be given to the Three Departments for public debate of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Send them to the Three Departments and debate the matter openly.

sentences.zh: 」初，同知樞密院範純仁以國用不足，建請復散青苗錢，四月之詔，蓋純仁意也。

translations.literal: 」Earlier, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Fan Chunren, because state revenues were insufficient, had proposed restoring disbursement of Green Sprouts money; the fourth-month edict was largely Chunren's idea.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fan Chunren of the Bureau of Military Affairs, citing empty coffers, had urged reviving Green Sprouts—the April edict was largely his doing.

sentences.zh: 時司馬光以疾在告，已而台諫皆言其非，不報。

translations.literal: At the time Sima Guang was on sick leave; soon censorial remonstrance officials all spoke against it—no response came.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang was then on sick leave. When censors and remonstrators objected, the court answered nothing.

sentences.zh: 光尋奏乞約束州縣抑配，蘇軾又繳奏，乞盡罷之。

translations.literal: Guang soon memorialized begging constraints on prefectural and county forced allocation; Su Shi again submitted a counter-memorial, begging complete abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang soon urged tighter limits on forced allocation; Su Shi submitted another memorial demanding full abolition.

sentences.zh: 光始大悟，遂力疾入對。

translations.literal: Guang then awoke greatly; thereupon despite illness he entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang finally saw the truth and dragged himself from sickbed to face the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋詔：「常平錢穀，止令州縣依舊法趁時糴糶，青苗錢更不支俵。

translations.literal: Soon an edict said: 「Ever-Normal money and grain—let prefectures and counties only follow the old law and buy and sell grain in season; Green Sprouts money shall no longer be disbursed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered counties to buy and sell Ever-Normal grain in season as before and to stop all Green Sprouts disbursements.

sentences.zh: 除舊欠二分之息，元支本錢驗見欠多少，分料次隨二稅輸納。」

translations.literal: Remit the old two-percent interest; verify how much principal originally borrowed remains owed, divide into installments, and pay with the two tax levies.」
translations.idiomatic: Waive outstanding two-percent interest; verify remaining principal and collect it in installments with the regular taxes.」

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，令州縣歲散常平錢穀畢，即揭示請人名數，逾月斂之，庶革偽冒之弊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuanhe, counties and prefectures were ordered: once annual Ever-Normal disbursement was finished, immediately post borrowers' names and numbers; collect after one month—thereby hopefully reforming the abuse of false claims.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 5 counties were told to post all borrowers' names after annual disbursement and collect after one month, to curb fraud.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸路災傷，截撥上供年額米斛數多，致闕中都歲計，令京東、江南、兩浙、荊湖路義倉穀各留三分，餘並起發赴京，補還截撥之數。

translations.literal: Earlier, on all circuits disaster losses had diverted much of the tribute grain quota, causing shortfall in the capital's annual budget; it was ordered that charity granary grain in the eastern capital, Jiangnan, two Zhe circuits, and Jinghu circuits each retain thirty percent, the rest dispatched to the capital to repay diverted amounts.
translations.idiomatic: After disasters had drained tribute grain and left the capital short, the court ordered charity granaries in the east, Jiangnan, two Zhes, and Jinghu to keep thirty percent locally and send the rest to the capital to make up diverted tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔罷之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the order was revoked.

sentences.zh: 孝宗隆興二年，遣司農少卿陳良弼點檢浙東常平等倉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longxing under Emperor Xiaozong, Vice Minister of Revenues Chen Liangbi was sent to inspect Ever-Normal and other granaries in eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 2 (1164) Chen Liangbi, vice minister of revenues, was dispatched to inspect Ever-Normal granaries in eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，知衢州胡堅奏廣糴常平。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao Prefect of Quzhou Hu Jian memorialized to expand Ever-Normal grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 6 the prefect of Quzhou, Hu Jian, asked to expand Ever-Normal grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 福建轉運副使沈樞奏，水旱州郡請留轉運司和糴米以續常平，上即為之施行。

translations.literal: Fujian Transport Deputy Commissioner Shen Shu memorialized: drought-and-flood prefectures begged to retain transport commission coordinated-purchase grain to replenish Ever-Normal; the Emperor immediately put it into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shu, Fujian's deputy transport commissioner, asked drought-stricken prefectures to keep coordinated-purchase grain for Ever-Normal reserves; the emperor approved at once.

sentences.zh: 八年，戶部侍郎楊倓奏：「義倉在法夏秋正稅鬥輸五合，不及鬥者免輸，凡豐熟縣九分以上即輸一升。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Tan memorialized: 「By law the charity granary takes five sheng per peck of summer and autumn principal tax; those owing less than a peck are exempt; in all bountiful counties nine-tenths or more pay one sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Vice Minister Yang Tan reported: 「Charity granaries legally levy five sheng per peck of summer and autumn tax; those owing less than a peck are exempt; in fertile counties the rate rises to one sheng per nine-tenths or more.

sentences.zh: 令諸路州縣歲收苗米六百餘萬石，其合收義倉米數不少，間有災傷，支給不多。

translations.literal: All circuit prefectures and counties now collect over six million piculs of seedling rice annually; the charity rice that should be collected is not small; yet when disaster occasionally strikes, disbursement is not much.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits collect over six million piculs of tax rice yearly—charity reserves should be substantial—yet when disaster strikes, payouts are meager.

sentences.zh: 訪聞諸州軍皆擅用，請稽之。」

translations.literal: I hear that all prefectures and garrisons use it on their own authority—I beg an audit.」
translations.idiomatic: I hear prefectures spend it freely—please investigate.」

sentences.zh: 寶慶三年，侍御史李知孝言：「郡縣素無蓄積，緩急止仰朝廷，非立法本意。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing Remonstrance Censor Li Zhixiao said: 「Prefectures and counties have never had reserves; in emergency they rely only on the court—this is not the original intent of the law.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoqing 3 Censor Li Zhixiao said: 「Local governments keep no reserves and lean on the court in crisis—that was never the law's purpose.

sentences.zh: 曩淮東總領岳珂任江東轉運判官，以所積經常錢糴米五萬石，樁留江東九郡，以時濟、糶，諸郡皆蒙其利。

translations.literal: Formerly when Huai-east General Controller Yue Ke served as Jiangdong Transport Vice Commissioner, he used accumulated routine funds to purchase fifty thousand piculs of rice, registered and retained them in Jiangdong's nine prefectures, timely relieving and selling grain—all prefectures benefited.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Ke was Jiangdong transport vice commissioner, he bought fifty thousand piculs with surplus funds and stored them across nine prefectures, selling and lending grain as needed—all benefited.

sentences.zh: 其後史彌忠知饒州，趙彥悈知廣德軍，皆自積錢糴米五千石。

translations.literal: Later Shi Mizhong as prefect of Raozhou and Zhao Yanjie as prefect of Guangde Army each accumulated funds and purchased five thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shi Mizhong in Raozhou and Zhao Yanjie in Guangde each bought five thousand piculs from local savings.

sentences.zh: 以是推之，監司、州郡苟能節用愛民，即有贏羨。

translations.literal: Inferring from this, if circuit supervisors and prefectures can economize and love the people, surplus will exist.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that thrift and care for the people will yield surpluses at every level.

sentences.zh: 若立之規繩，加以黜陟，所糴至萬石者旌擢，其不收糴與擾民及不實者鐫罰，庶幾郡縣趨事，蓄積歲增，實為經久之利。

translations.literal: If regulations are set and promotions and demotions applied—those purchasing up to ten thousand piculs honored and promoted, those failing to purchase, harassing the people, or reporting falsely punished by inscription—then perhaps prefectures and counties will hurry to the task, reserves increase year by year, truly a lasting benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Set rules with rewards and punishments—promote those who stock ten thousand piculs, penalize those who hoard, harass, or falsify records—and counties will build reserves year by year for lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 」有旨從之。

translations.literal: 」An imperial directive followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 景定元年九月，赦曰：「諸路已糶義米價錢，州郡以低價抑令上戶補糴，正稅逃閣，義米用虧，常平司責縣道陪納，縣道遂敷吏貼、保正長、攬戶等人均納。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingding a pardon edict said: 「On all circuits charity rice already sold for cash—prefectures at low prices forced wealthy households to make up purchases; principal tax was evaded and deferred; charity rice use ran short; Ever-Normal office held counties liable for replacement payment; counties then assessed clerks, ward chiefs, and tax brokers equally.
translations.idiomatic: A Jingding 1 (1260) amnesty condemned a common abuse: after charity rice was sold for cash, prefectures forced wealthy households to buy grain at low prices to refill stores. Tax evasion left charity stocks empty; Ever-Normal offices held counties liable, and counties spread the cost across clerks, ward chiefs, and tax brokers.

sentences.zh: 自今視時收糴，見係吏貼等人陪納之錢並與除放。

translations.literal: From now purchase grain according to season; all replacement payments still owed by clerks and others are remitted.」
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth purchase grain in season, and remit all outstanding replacement payments owed by clerks and others.」

sentences.zh: 」五年，監察御史程元嶽奏：「隨粳帶義，法也。

translations.literal: 」In the fifth year Investigating Censor Cheng Yuanyue memorialized: 「Attaching charity levy to hulled rice is the law.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Censor Cheng Yuanyue wrote: 「The law ties the charity levy to hulled rice alone.

sentences.zh: 今粳糯帶義之外，又有所謂外義焉者，絹、綢、豆也，豈有絹、綢、豆而可加之義乎？

translations.literal: Now beyond hulled and glutinous rice with charity levy, there is so-called outer charity on silk, satin, and beans—can silk, satin, and beans have charity added to them?
translations.idiomatic: Yet beyond rice, officials impose so-called outer charity on silk, satin, and beans—how can charity attach to cloth and legumes?

sentences.zh: 縱使違法加義，則絹加絹，綢加綢，豆加豆，猶可言也；

translations.literal: Even if unlawfully adding charity, then silk adding silk, satin adding satin, beans adding beans might still be spoken of;
translations.idiomatic: Even illegal surcharges should at least match the commodity—silk on silk, beans on beans;

sentences.zh: 州縣一意椎剝，一切理苗而加一分之義，甚者赦恩已蠲二稅，義米依舊追索。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties single-mindedly squeeze and strip, treating all seedling assessments and adding one-tenth charity; in extreme cases, after amnesty pardoned the two taxes, charity rice was still pursued for collection.
translations.idiomatic: But counties squeeze every tax item with a ten-percent charity markup—and even after amnesties wipe the two main levies, charity rice is still collected.

sentences.zh: 貧民下戶所欠不過升合，星火追呼，費用不知幾百倍。

translations.literal: Poor people and lower households owed no more than sheng and he; urgent pursuit came like sparks—costs were unknowably hundreds of times greater.
translations.idiomatic: The poor owed mere handfuls of grain, yet urgent collection cost them hundreds of times more.

sentences.zh: 破家蕩產，鬻妻子，怨嗟之聲，有不忍聞。

translations.literal: Families were ruined and estates emptied; wives and children were sold; the sound of lamentation—some could not bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Families were ruined, wives and children sold—the cries of despair were unbearable.

sentences.zh: 望嚴督監司，止許以粳帶義，其餘盡罷。

translations.literal: I hope to strictly supervise circuit overseers—only allow charity attached to hulled rice; abolish all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: I urge strict oversight: charity levy on hulled rice only—all other surcharges abolished.

sentences.zh: 其有循習病民者重其罰。

translations.literal: Those who persist in old habits harming the people—heavily punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Punish harshly any official who persists in these abuses.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 咸淳二年，以諸路景定三年以前常平義倉米二百餘萬石，減時直糶之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianchun, over two million piculs of Ever-Normal and charity granary rice from before Jingding year three on all circuits were sold at reduced current prices.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun 2 more than two million piculs of Ever-Normal and charity rice hoarded since before Jingding 3 were sold at reduced market prices empire-wide.
